News.title: Death row killer Christa Pike’s second little-known crime as murderer carried out brutal attack with shoelace
News.content:
Next

DEATH row killer Christa Pike attempted a second grisly murder while serving a life sentence in prison.

Pike, who remains in hospital after surviving two doses of lethal injection, was found guilty of attempted murder for the little- known crime in 2001.



The 50-year-old has been left unable to breath on her own after the failed execution attempt earlier this week.

If successful, Pike would have been the first woman in Tennessee to be executed in over 200 years.



Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the brutal murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.

She carried out the deadly attack with her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, who Pike said Slemmer was trying to steal from her.

Read More on Christa Pike FIGHT FOR LIFE Christa Pike's health & disturbing new details of botched execution revealed



Carved with satanic pentagrams and badly beaten, Colleen’s corpse was first mistaken for an animal.

Pike has never denied killing Slemmer but said she was “a mentally ill 18-year-old kid”.



She has been on death row at Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville since she was convicted in 1996.

While in prison in 2001, she tried to kill fellow inmate Patricia Jones, by strangling her with a shoestring.

She was convicted of attempted first-degree murder in 2004.

Five years later two men were arrested in a plot to break Pike out of jail.

“We thwarted it in its infant stages,” said Kristin Helm, spokesperson for the bureau at the time. “It would have been nearly impossible to carry out.”



Former prison guard Justin Heflin was indicted for his part in the foiled attempt and Pike’s then-boyfriend Donald Kohut was also charged.

In recent weeks Pike’s lawyers have tried to stop the execution, arguing that her crime could not be separated from her traumatic childhood.

Her legal team previously petitioned the governor to commute her sentence to life without parole.



It pointed to evidence that her mother drank heavily during pregnancy, impairing Pike’s brain development and her impulse control.

Her clemency petition documents childhood violence, neglect and sexual abuse, including rapes when she was aged 11 and 17.

Her lawyers maintain that the Christa Pike of today is not the volatile teenager of 1995.

They recently said: “With time and treatment, Christa has become a thoughtful woman with deep remorse for her crime.”

Her botched execution now creates extraordinary questions over whether Tennessee can legally attempt to execute her again.



Pike remained “critically ill” as of Thursday night, and was “intubated, on a ventilator, and remains unconscious,” the filing said.

Hospital workers have been working tirelessly to save Pike’s life and clear the lethal drug from her system.

Her arms remain burned, blistered and swollen after her attorneys say she was struck with at least seven needles.

Her lawyers raised concerns about lethal injection months before her day of execution, saying she had small veins and a blood condition that could make it more difficult to insert an IV.

What comes next remains unclear, as Dr Joel Zivot – a medical advisor to Pike’s legal team – told The Sun there are situations where an inmate is took sick to be put to death.



He said if Pike’s heath “can never be restored to some degree where it would be conceivable that she could actually be executed again, then she may not face that.”

However, if she recovers to a certain degree, there is a chance she could face a second execution attempt, Zivot said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has pressed pause on the remaining executions scheduled for 2026 after officials were unable to carry out Pike’s execution.

Lee has demanded a review of the state’s execution procedures as well.

News.title: Chilling footage shows moment balaclava-clad men ambush man, 21, like ‘pack of animals’ before stabbing him to death
News.content:
Next

TERRIFYING footage shows a group of balaclava-clad knifemen ambushing a 21-year-old like a “pack of animals” before brutally stabbing him to death.

Chilling CCTV shows the gang – who were yesterday jailed for more than a century – surrounding Dale Martin after blocking his car.



The group, riding electric bikes, then dragged him out and launched a frenzied knife attack.

Dale was brutally murdered on Stenson Road in Derby on June 15, 2025 – leading to a major manhunt, including arrests made at the airport as some culprits attempted to flee abroad.



The six-strong gang had tracked the victim down following a “tit-for-tat” feud between rival groups.

They surrounded Dale as he travelled in a Renault Megane before dragging him from the vehicle.





Armed with swords, machetes and Rambo-style knives, the thugs then attacked him as he tried to escape.

The court heard they chopped at Dale’s head, chest and back after he fell to the ground.

CCTV captured the gang travelling on their electric bikes moments before the attack.

It also showed them fleeing the scene afterwards, leaving Dale dying in the street.



The group were heard shouting “kill him, kill him” as they carried out what prosecutors described as a “brutal, sustained, and planned attack”.

Blood was later found splattered across Dale’s Renault after the horror assault.



The killing triggered a huge manhunt and eventually led to the arrests of multiple people, including the six who were accused of Dale’s murder.

Following a four-month trial a jury took more than two weeks to convict six men of his killing.



Jayden Mannion-Roberts was found guilty of his murder and has now been jailed for life and must serve a minimum of 27 years before being eligible for parole.

Ki Grant-Finlayson and Keenan Hamblett were arrested just as they were about to board a flight to Tunisia a few days after the murder.

They were both found guilty of manslaughter.

Grant-Finlayson was jailed for 18 years, with an extended licence period of 21 years, while Hamblett received a 17 years and six months term.



Kelci Thompson, Shaylon McCalla and Kayin Holmes were also found guilty of manslaughter.

McCalla, who was arrested after flying into Birmingham International Airport, was given an 18-year sentence, with an extended licence period of 21 years.

Holmes was jailed for 15 years, while Thompson was jailed for 10 years.



All but Mannion-Roberts must serve at least two thirds of their sentence before they are able to be released.

Temporary Detective Inspector Chris Wright said: “The killing of Dale Martin was a planned, sustained, and brutal attack.

“The group had set out that night with the intention of causing Dale serious harm – and they carried out their wishes armed with knives and machetes.

“Dale was pulled from a car, chased and fatally stabbed multiple times.

“All those convicted in relation to this offence were happy to use really serious violence in a residential street, with no concern for the harm they would cause, or the worry they would generate in the community.



“The investigation into this crime would not have been possible without the help of the public and I would like to thank them for their support – their assistance was vital in gathering the evidence to bring those responsible to justice.

“I also want to thank Dale’s family for their support during what has been a long journey to get to court – and then an extended trial which has included distressing information that no family should have to hear.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Finally, I would like to express my thanks to the investigation team and wider force.

“The response to this incident covered almost every area of the force – on both a direct and indirect level.”

News.title: Shocking moment huge bear with cub attacks car and bites vehicle as horrified driver desperately locks the doors
News.content:
Next

THIS is the terrifying moment a massive bear attacks a car, sinking its teeth into the bonnet as the driver scrambles to lock her doors.

Heart-stopping dashcam footage shows the bear and its cub suddenly emerge from the darkness directly before violently attacking the vehicle.



The driver – a woman in her 30s – slammed on her brakes but the larger animal, believed to be the mother, suddenly charged at speed.

The crazed animal launched itself onto the car before repeatedly battering the bonnet with its powerful paws.



It briefly backs away before changing course and attacking again but this time biting the vehicle.

Terrified inside, the woman desperately locked her doors and waited for the animal to leave, left wondering if she was a sitting duck.



The terrifying encounter occurred on Tuesday evening as the woman drove home from work on the Japanese island of Hokkaido.

She said: “I stopped because I thought I was going to hit them, and then it attacked.



“I locked the doors and prayed it wouldn’t get inside and waited for it to go away.”

The woman said she could feel the car shaking and hear the animal growling outside as she feared the beast would break through the glass.

Police said the two animals appeared to be a parent and cub.

The larger bear was estimated to be around 1.5m long, while local reports put the cub at approximately one metre.

The force of the assault left the bonnet dented and covered in deep claw marks.



Some of the bear’s claws even punched holes straight through the metal.

Despite the damage, the car remained driveable and the woman escaped without injury before making her way to a police station.

The two bears eventually disappeared back towards the forest.

Police have stepped up patrols around the area following the frightening encounter.

Authorities said the road is in a mountainous area around 10km from central Bifuka where bear sightings are frequently reported.



The latest local figures show police have received 55 reports relating to brown bears across Hokkaido in the space of just one week.

Drivers have been urged to remain vigilant, particularly when travelling through rural areas at night.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In June, a man was mauled to death by a bear amid a sharp rise in bear activity across Japan.

According to the environmental industry of Japan, six people have been killed by bears since April.

News.title: Plane carrying six people goes missing after taking off from Bermuda as US Coast Guard launches desperate search
News.content:
AIR MYSTERY Plane carrying six people goes missing after taking off from Bermuda as US Coast Guard launches desperate search







Next

A PLANE carrying six people has vanished after taking off from Bermuda on Saturday morning.

The US Coast Guard confirmed that it has launched a search for the craft and those onboard.



It noted in its statement on X that the Federal Aviation Administration lost contact with a Bermuda-Boston Gulfstream aircraft in the early hours.

“USGC air and surface crews have launched in search of the aircraft,” it said.



The search is currently focused off the coast of Nantucket, Massachusetts.

Officials confirmed that the aircraft is a Gulfstream G100 with tail number CGRJP.



No further information has yet been released.

It comes just weeks after a family of four were found dead after their plane went missing in the Bermuda Triangle on the way to Miami, Florida.

Florida couple Mario Lamar, 80, and Lili Lamar, 79, were traveling with their grandchildren Sofi Sosa, 28, and Christian Sosa, 22, when their plane crashed near Andros Islands, the largest in the Bahamas.

News.title: Woman’s body found on popular UK beach after coastguard and lifeboat crews seen searching water
News.content:

BEACH TRAGEDY Woman’s body found on popular UK beach after coastguard and lifeboat crews seen searching water







Next

A WOMAN’S body has been found at a popular UK beach today after search and rescue teams scoured the sea.

The grim discovery was made this morning at 8.18am as emergency services and several police cars rushed to Marine Parade at Eastbourne beach.



It is understood that an RNLI helicopter sprung into action at 3.30pm on Thursday after a welfare concern was made.

The woman’s body was found on the shoreline, reportedly wearing a wetsuit.



Police officers were seen gathering around her, holding up sheets to shield her from the view of onlookers.

The woman’s family have been informed of the tragedy.



In a statement, Sussex Police said: “We were called to a report of a body of a woman found on the beach by Marine Parade, Eastbourne, at about 8.18am on Saturday (October 3).

“The death is not being treated as suspicious and her next of kin have been informed.

“A report is being prepared for HM coroner.”

A spokesperson for the RNLI said: “Solent Coastguard requested our volunteer crew to assist with a multi-agency search after unattended items had been located towards the west of Eastbourne.



“The ILB carried out a shoreline search alongside local Coastguard Rescue Teams, the coastguard helicopter ‘Rescue 363’ and Sussex Police officers.”

News.title: We live in King Charles’ ‘Wild West’ uni town forced to bring in BOOZE BAN – drunks turned streets into ‘no-go’ zones
News.content:
'WILD WEST' We live in King Charles’ ‘Wild West’ uni town forced to bring in BOOZE BAN – drunks turned streets into ‘no-go’ zones







Next

A UNI town where King Charles once studied is cracking down on booze after residents complained about being menaced by “drunken men”.

Locals told The Sun they back an extension to a ban on street drinking saying the seaside town had been blighted by antisocial drunks.



Aberystwyth University, previously the University College of Wales, famously hosted King Charles for a single 10-week-term in 1969.

He studied Welsh lanuage and Welsh history to prepare for his formal investiture as the Prince of Wales at Caernarfon Castle.



But the town had been branded the “Wild West“, along with Cardigan and Lampeter, after reports of drunken men and wolf-whistling.

The council has now slapped on Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs), which allow the banning of drinking alcohol in designated public areas.



Under restrictions, it is an offence to ignore a police or authorised officer’s request to stop drinking or to surrender alcohol.

Failure to comply with the rules can warrant an on-the-spot Fixed Penalty Notice of £100, which can be extended to a maximum fine of £1,000.

Ceris, a 19 year-old student, is one of many at who were celebrating after the local council first slapped a ban on drinking in public.

Ceris said: “There’s nothing I like more after lectures or studying in the library than lacing up and running around the town, especially along the promenade because it is so beautiful.



“But so often those runs have been spoiled by the behaviour of men under the influence of alcohol.

“They will be sitting outside pubs or on the beach near the promenade and when I run by they’ll start wolf whistling.

“It feels really threatening and I am uncomfortable with it. Usually, I’ll make sure I’m on the other side of the road or even sometimes I’ve changed my route completely just to avoid them, but why should I?”

Her friend Lauryn, a 20-year-old geography student at the university, said: “Very often I won’t even go out now because of the way men behave when they’re drinking outside, away from the scrutiny of bar staff and doormen.



“I’ll just stay indoors at home and have a drink with my friends instead because it feels safer.

“It’s a really scary when you’re on your own and you have to walk past a group of men drinking.”

The Welsh town is known for its stunning sea-front and friendly atmosphere, but thanks to drinking culture, has left some areas a “no-go” zone at night.

Jackie, 74, said she would love to be spending a sunny afternoon in Aberystwyth drinking a large gin and tonic outdoors with magnificent sea views in front of her.



“But as always, a tiny minority of people, in this case drunken men, have spoiled it for all of us.

“If men can’t behave themselves properly when they’ve had a drink, then this has to be the way forward, unfortunately.“

Her husband, Paul, 76, agreed. He said: “Most men know how to behave themselves properly when they’ve had a drink, but some do get a bit too drunk and behave in an antisocial way.

“Anything that gives women greater protection when they’re out is good with me.”



And retired NHS worker Colin, 65, said: “If you walk down to the beach on a sunny summer evening, you can see large groups of men congregating and drinking can after can of beer.

“That is incredibly intimidating for women and frankly it’s a public nuisance.

“Their behaviour is totally antisocial and it leaves a mess for others to clear up. Places like the beach or areas outside bars at night should never become no go areas for anybody. Well done to the council.”

According to Alun Williams, councillor for Aberystwyth Morfa a Glais, “drunk men were dominating the centre of Aberystwyth” before the ban, creating a “wild west intimidating atmosphere”.

In the past year, Dyfed-Powys Police Local Commander said it recorded a “relatively low number of recorded incidents” where street drinking was a contributing factor to incidents



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Despite the lowering incidence, members recently unanimously backed the extension in all three towns, with Williams continuing: “Let’s not throw away a policy that is working and has clear support.”

The council has further said that the PSPOs will continue to be regularly reviewed in line with key stakeholders and analysis of police data.

News.title: Putin regime in ‘cover-up’ over ‘Black Death outbreak as one dead and 189 in isolation’ amid fears of new pandemic
News.content:
Next

VLADIMIR Putin has been accused of covering up a “plague” outbreak which has killed one person and force another 189 into quarantine.

Putin’s chief infectious diseases doctor Anna Popova rushed 2,600 miles from Moscow to Irkutsk in Siberia to take personal charge of the emergency – but has remained silent.



Daria Shipilova, 28, a “specialist” at Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Irkutsk, is reported to have died from the deadly bubonic plague.

Reports now say 189 people are in isolation – 114 are in one hospital, 63 in another, and another 12 are at the Anti-Plague Research Institute.



Meanwhile the regional governor Igor Kobzev has refused to name what he called a “dangerous infectious disease”, as he cancelled mass events in the region.

Antibiotics have already run out in the Irkutsk region as terrified residents flocked to pharmacies, said reports.



And residents of neighbouring Baikalsk were told to avoid travelling to Shelekhov in an official notice that was later deleted.

Russian news outlet Mash said: “Doctors and Rospotrebnadzor [Russia’s public health watchdog] are investigating the circumstances of the infection and carrying out anti-epidemic measures.”



But officials, including Popova, are still refusing to comment on the specifics of the disease.

Political insider channel Nezygar has compared the case to China when Covid broke out.

“The situation in Shelekhov, Irkutsk region, where a plague quarantine has been declared, resembles the Wuhan case,” warned the outlet.

Daria reportedly worked for an “anti-plague institute” when she fell ill while on an expedition on the border between Russia and Mongolia where fast-spreading infections were confirmed.

She was raced to the Shelekhov District Hospital which has now been placed under quarantine.



“Some of them have symptoms of the disease,” said political insider channel Nezygar, although this claim has not been officially confirmed

It remains unclear how Daria first contracted the deadly plague.

One theory in Russian media claims she accidentally broke a test tube containing a “dangerous bacterium” in a lab using biological material for diagnostic testing.



But senior Russian epidemiologist Mikhail Favorov – now living in the US – said: “The story about the test tube? It’s laughable….

“Someone working at the anti-plague institute in Irkutsk wears a protective anti-plague suit.

“If you break a test tube, the likelihood of infection is actually very low.

“In short, it doesn’t matter to the general public. They’ll believe the ‘dropped test tube’ story.”

Popova’s personal presence in Irkutsk meant it is a “terrible, critical situation”, Mikhail added.



There is speculation that Daria may have believed she was suffering from coronavirus.

“I rather doubt she was treated with antibiotics,” said Mikhail.

If prescribed early these could have saved her.

Mikhail added: “It seems to me they diagnosed her with COVID because she was having trouble breathing and put her on a ventilator. It’s absolutely hair-raising.”

This may have led to the potential infection of many others.



He suggested a major cover-up was underway, saying: “We will not be told what really happened.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The last registered case of the plague in Russia was in 2016, where a 10-year-old boy who was skinning a marmot carcass became infected.

The bacterial disease was responsible for the notorious medieval Black Death.

News.title: Russia unleashes fresh Kyiv bridge strike in bid to cripple life in war-torn capital
News.content:
Russia unleashes fresh Kyiv bridge strike in bid to cripple life in war-torn capital

Two people were injured in the Kremlin's attack on the Northern Bridge early on Saturday, which comes after Moscow strikes on Southern Bridge in Kyiv this week

View 4 Images Vladimir Putin's Russia launched its full-scale invasion of neighbour Ukraine over four-and-a-half years ago (Image: Sergei Bobylev/Pool Sputnik Krem)

Russia has unleashed a fresh bridge strike on Kyiv as Moscow bids to cripple life in war-torn Ukraine’s capital.

‌



‌



Two people were injured when a Kremlin attack damaged Kyiv’s Northern Bridge early on Saturday. The hit came after Russia attacked the city’s Southern Bridge, over the Dnipro River, this week. Vitali Klitschko, the city’s mayor, earlier this week warned Moscow’s intensified strikes were “tearing Kyiv apart”. On Saturday, Mr Klitschko said the bridge strike damaged the road surface and trolleybus cables, with westbound traffic suspended. Two people were hurt, including one who was hospitalised, he said. Videos circulating on social media appeared to show the moment of impact as vehicles crossed the bridge

‌



View 4 Images Technicians repair a trolleybus power line after Russian attack on the Northern Bridge in Kyiv on October 3 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Kyiv defies Trump with massive drone barrage against Russian oil READ MORE :

Russia's Defence Ministry confirmed it was behind the latest attack, claiming the bridge is used to "facilitate troop movements and the logistics of military cargo deliveries" for Ukraine's armed forces.

Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of neighbour Ukraine over four-and-a-half years ago. The aerial war has intensified, with Kyiv striking Russia's oil industry and businesses. Meanwhile, the Kremlin has menaced Ukrainian cities with hard-to-intercept ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones.

‌



View 4 Images Traces of the explosion on a pedestrian way after the attack on the Northern Bridge in Kyiv on October 3 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Volodymyr Zelensky this week told how Ukrainian spy agencies had obtained info that Vladimir Putin had scrapped the constraints governing earlier air campaigns. The Ukrainian president told the Financial Times: “He said there are no rules now.” Putin gave the order last month, Zelensky said, as Moscow began intensifying air strikes on Ukraine’s capital.

On Saturday, the president of Moldova, which borders Ukraine, said the war is "dangerously reaching" her country, following a spate of airspace incursions. Maia Sandu said: “I condemn Russia's attack on Ukraine this morning. Its war is dangerously reaching Moldova. 5 Russian air attack weapons, including Banderol missiles and drones, violated our airspace and exploded on our soil. Moscow is putting lives at risk across Europe and must be stopped.”

Article continues below

View 4 Images Technicians repair a trolleybus power line damaged following an attack on the Northern Bridge in Kyiv on October 3 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Ukraine's air force said that Moscow overnight into Saturday launched Banderol cruise missiles – low-cost, jet-powered loitering munitions that Russia uses to overwhelm Ukrainian air defences – at the Odesa region, which shares a long land border with Moldova.

A loitering munition is designed to hover over an area, searching for targets, and detonate while crashing into them.

News.title: FlyDubai - live: Co-pilot Hamam al Hammami who 'attacked captain' had studied with UK uni
News.content:
Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, is alleged to have tried to hijack a FlyDubai plane with 182 people on board after attacking the captain before passengers helped to subdue him

A FlyDubai co-pilot alleged to have attacked the captain on an Israel-bound flight with an axe before attempting to hijack the plane had completed an aviation course at a UK university.

Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, is alleged to have hit Captain Smit Machchhar with the weapon on the flight to Tel Aviv and tried to seize the jet's controls. He is alleged to have been barred from flying in Oman over concerns he had adopted extremist views, a source familiar with the subject said.

Buckinghamshire New University, based in High Wycombe, has confirmed al-Hammami studied with them and had "previously completed a distance-learning course in aviation management". A spokesman added: "He did not undertake any pilot training at the University".

Al-Hammami's alleged actions nearly crashed the flight with 182 people on board on Wednesday before passengers and others rushed in and subdued him.

United Arab Emirates officials have called what happened a "terrorist" incident in a statement that cited the UAE attorney general.

News.title: New wet wipe ban coming soon across UK as part of major law change
News.content:
New wet wipe ban coming soon across UK as part of major law change

Wales will be the first to implement the major change, with other UK nations to follow

View 3 Images The major change is hoped to help tackle a problematic environmental issue (stock image) (Image: Getty)

A major ban on single-use wet wipes containing plastic is set to roll out across all four UK nations over the next year. The ban will mark a stark change in how people clean, remove makeup, and care for babies.

‌



‌



The new laws aim to tackle a major cause of environmental pollution, as plastic wet wipes do not break down when flushed. Trillions of plastic fibres from discarded wipes end up clogging sewage systems, creating notorious "fatbergs, and polluting marine ecosystems when flushed down toilets.

‌



Because environmental laws are managed independently by each devolved government, the restrictions will take effect on different dates across the regions. Below is a summary of when the changes are expected to be made, with Wales first.

‌



Wales: December 18, 2026

December 18, 2026 Northern Ireland: May 18, 2027

May 18, 2027 England: May 19, 2027

May 19, 2027 Scotland: August 11, 2027

View 3 Images Plastic wet wipes will be disappearing off shop shelves soon

Once the deadlines pass, retailers won't be allowed to sell or supply traditional plastic-based single-use wipes. The restriction covers everyday items such as baby wipes, facial cleansing sheets, household cleaning wipes, and moist toilet tissues.

‌



What type of wet wipes will be affected?

The ban applies to the online and in-store sale or supply of the following plastic-containing items:

Baby and child care

Baby wipes: Traditional plastic-based wipes used for nappies and regular cleaning.

Traditional plastic-based wipes used for nappies and regular cleaning. Toddler wipes: Hand and face wipes designed for young children.

‌



Cosmetics and skincare

Makeup removal wipes: Cleansing wipes for removing makeup and mascara.

Cleansing wipes for removing makeup and mascara. Face wipes: General exfoliating, toning, or refreshing face cloths.

General exfoliating, toning, or refreshing face cloths. Cosmetic face sheet masks: Single-use, pre-moistened fabric masks soaked in skincare serums.

Personal hygiene

‌



Moist toilet tissue: Pre-wetted wipes intended for use after using the toilet (including many currently marketed as "flushable").

Pre-wetted wipes intended for use after using the toilet (including many currently marketed as "flushable"). Antibacterial hand wipes: Sanitising wipes for cleaning hands on the go.

Sanitising wipes for cleaning hands on the go. Deodorant and body wipes: Personal hygiene sheets used to freshen up or reduce sweat.

Personal hygiene sheets used to freshen up or reduce sweat. Intimate hygiene wipes: Wipes formulated for specific personal care needs.

Household and surface cleaning

Household cleaning wipes: Surface disinfectant wipes, kitchen counter wipes, and bathroom cleaning cloths.

Surface disinfectant wipes, kitchen counter wipes, and bathroom cleaning cloths. Wet-mop wipes: Pre-soaked disposable cleaning pads designed to fit onto floor mops.

‌



View 3 Images Biodegradable and plastic-free wipes will still be allowed

Will all wet wipes disappear from shelves?

However, wet wipes will not disappear entirely from store shelves. Shoppers will still be able to buy reusable alternatives and single-use wipes made strictly from biodegradable, plastic-free materials such as bamboo or plant fibres.

The legislation does include some exemptions, however. Plastic-containing wipes will still be allowed for professional medical treatment, industrial manufacturing, and laboratory use.

‌



And although high-street shops won't be allowed to display them, registered pharmacies will be allowed to supply them over the counter to people who require them for specific health needs. The exemption exists because plastic fibres give wipes unique properties, such as high durability, chemical compatibility, and superior moisture retention, that are critical in specific care scenarios.

The government is advising businesses to prepare for the upcoming ban by reviewing their inventories. Selling banned stock after the regional deadlines could result in hefty financial penalties.

Article continues below

Why are plastic wet wipes being banned?

Plastic wet wipes are being banned because they do not break down when flushed, causing catastrophic blockages that account for 94% of UK sewer clogs and costing an estimated £200 million annually to clear. Instead of dissolving like toilet paper, these plastic-laced wipes bind with grease to form massive underground fatbergs, causing raw sewage to overflow into homes and rivers.

They accumulate in massive quantities on UK coastlines and riverbeds, slowly degrading into toxic microplastics that contaminate the marine food chain and poison aquatic wildlife.

News.title: 'Doctors repeatedly told me it was nothing to worry about - then I got horror diagnosis'
News.content:
'Doctors repeatedly told me it was nothing to worry about - then I got horror diagnosis'

EXCLUSIVE: Sophie Cohn, 17, said her concerns were repeatedly dismissed by a doctor, and was even told to wait and see if her period restarted before she was diagnosed with cancer

View 6 Images Sophie Cohn said her concerns were dismissed after she took them to a doctor (Image: Cover Images)

A teenage girl has said doctors dismissed her health concerns due to her age — before she was diagnosed with cancer aged just 17.

‌



‌



When Sophie Cohn noticed she had stopped getting her period, she went to visit her GP. But her missed periods were attributed to her age and the stress of being a busy teenager at school. But six months later, Sophie still had not had a period and returned to the doctor — yet was given more of the same advice and to wait and see if it came back.

‌



Her period did not return and Sophie, from Hertfordshire, became noticeably tired and felt unfit in the weeks which followed. She said: "I went back to the GP in June and said, ‘Hey, something still isn't right here. I still have no period'.

‌



"And then he just told me the same thing saying, 'You've got the summer off, see if it comes back, you won't be stressed with school anymore'."

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Dignity in Dying vow to fight bill knockback in Dame Esther Rantzen’s honour READ MORE :

BBC Breakfast pays tribute to 'extraordinary' Dame Esther Rantzen as broadcaster dies READ MORE :

View 6 Images Sophie said she was told to 'see if it comes back' when she raised fears over her absent periods (Image: Cover Images)

‌



By September of that year - 2019, when Sophie was 17 - she had gone about nine months without a period. Her GP prescribed medication to ‘kick start’ it, but when her period came she experienced severe stomach pain.

Speaking to the Mirror, Sophie said: “I found towards the end of the summer, I was getting very tired, and I felt like I was very unfit, but then I put that down to being away all summer, and going out a lot. He (a doctor) gave me the pills, I took them, my period came, I then got the worst stomach pains I have ever had."

As her pain got worse, Sophie’s parents contacted a gastroenterologist who lived a few doors down, who told them to take her straight to A&E. It was there, almost nine months after she first realised something was wrong, that doctors began investigating what would eventually lead to a diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma.

‌



View 6 Images Sophie said pills that returned her period also caused severe cramping (Image: Cover Images)

Looking back, Sophie wonders whether her initial concerns should have been taken more seriously.

The young woman, who works in sustainability, added: “I'm not saying that when I first went to the GP and I stopped getting my period it meant that I had cancer, I'm never going to know that. But it was my body telling me something was wrong.”

‌



Sophie believes her age and gender may have influenced how her symptoms were perceived. She added: "I do think it's partly to do with my age, and a lot of the time, I think doctors tend to put a lot of issues that women and girls have when they're in their teens down to periods and hormones."

But even after reaching hospital, Sophie’s diagnosis was not straightforward. Doctors carried out blood tests and a chest X-ray, finding she was severely anaemic with a slightly high white blood cell count.

Sophie said she was initially told the results were otherwise normal and sent home. She added: "They said I was severely anaemic and referred me to someone to sort that out. Other than that, they said that my bloods were fine, my chest x-ray was normal… ‘it's all normal, you can go home’.”

‌



But a week later, her mum received a call from the hospital.

"My mum got a call saying someone else had reviewed my chest x-ray, I need to come in immediately. So, she called me while I was at school and she said, ‘We need to go to the hospital.’”

Doctors told Sophie they were concerned she could have picked up an illness during a recent trip to South Africa and began investigating three possible conditions: tuberculosis, sarcoidosis or lymphoma.

‌



View 6 Images Sophie was diagnosed with Hodgkins Lymphoma (Image: Cover Images)

“People were coming in wearing masks, and this was pre-Covid, and I asked, ‘Why are you wearing masks? What is happening?’ And no one was telling me anything. But they said either way, 'there's something in your chest'."

Weeks later, doctors attempted a biopsy but were unable to sedate Sophie because she was too anaemic, but that was not communicated to her. She was referred to London, where surgeons cut into the side of her ribcage to perform the biopsy under general anaesthetic.

‌



Another week later, Sophie was given the news that she had Hodgkin lymphoma. Doctors initially believed it was stage two, but further tests at a teenage cancer unit revealed it had progressed to stage four and had spread. Sophie began six months of gruelling chemotherapy, spending five days a week travelling to London for treatment while dealing with nausea, "horrendous" stomach pain, shooting pains in her legs and extreme tiredness.

The treatment was made even harder as Sophie was still recovering from a biopsy that was not healing properly due to her compromised immune system. Her hair began falling out just 10 days into treatment. Sophie said: "That was probably the worst, because that was the biggest physical sign of, understanding that, yeah, I'm ill now." Sophie was also missing out on school and normal teenage activities.

“I couldn't go to any crowded places or parties, because my immune system was so bad. I would go to school, but I would go in for my lessons and then I would go home again."

‌



View 6 Images Sophie's hair started falling out 10 days into treatment (Image: Cover Images)

By June 2020, Sophie had finished the intense course of treatment and was officially in remission and she and her family could finally breathe a sigh of relief. But she still wonders whether her cancer could have been caught earlier had her symptoms been taken more seriously.

“I try not to think about it too much, but stage one cancer is a lot better than stage four. By the time that I had my PET scan, it was all over my body.

‌



"It was in my spleen, so I have to take lifelong antibiotics now because the radiotherapy essentially radiated my spleen, so it doesn't work properly. So, I sometimes wonder, could I have had two months of chemotherapy instead of six."

The experience also took a heavy toll on Sophie’s mental health, something she says she did not fully recognise until afterwards.

“I was of the mindset of just get through this. You have six months of this and then you can kind of think about your feelings on the other side. There's no time to deal with feelings now.”

Article continues below

Although Sophie had emotional moments during treatment, she largely pushed her feelings aside to focus on getting through it.

View 6 Images Sophie said she spent time in therapy following her experience with cancer (Image: Cover Images)

Sophie, now 24, said: “Obviously, I did still cry. But, not as much as you would have thought I would. And then, the years following, there was lots of therapy and lots of coming to terms with what I went through.” Now, Sophie is advocating for greater awareness of cancer symptoms in young people. She added: “The symptoms can be quite ordinary, and they're symptoms that I would brush off, or my parents would brush off. It is easy to just put it down to being a teenager who's going out too much. “But if a doctor hears those symptoms, they should take it a bit more seriously, so you don't have to go back three times and feel like you're being really silly.” For Sophie, the hope is that other young people will be listened to before their symptoms have a chance to become something more serious.

News.title: Labour candidate who fled Somalia as a child praises refugees impact on Britain
News.content:
Labour candidate who fled Somalia as a child praises refugees impact on Britain

EXCLUSIVE Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee from Somalia, said she was 'inspired' Ed Miliband, who had discussed how his parents had fled persecution to come to the UK

View 2 Images Sagal Abdi-Wali is a former child refugee from Somalia (Image: Tim Merry/Staff Photographer)

Labour’s candidate in Keir Starmer's old seat has praised Ed Miliband’s conference speech for showing “refugees come from all backgrounds” and bring “so much” to Britain.

‌



Sagal Abdi-Wali, a former child refugee from Somalia, said she was “inspired” by the Foreign Secretary’s address in Liverpool, in which he discussed how his parents had fled persecution to come to the UK.

The Labour candidate in the Holborn and St Pancras, who has faced criticism from Reform's Zia Yusuf over not being born in Britain, also hit out at the “divisive” rhetoric used by Suella Braverman after she was accused of suggesting that non-white people cannot be English.

Speaking to this newspaper, she said: “I was really inspired by it and touched by it. He's come down a couple of times and we've spoken about it.

View 2 Images Sagal Abdi-Wali is running in Keir Starmer's old seat (Image: Tim Merry/Staff Photographer)

“Last time he was here we spoke about how much his mother influenced his political thinking and his outlook on life and what he wants to do in terms of the Foreign Secretary brief.

“He's obviously starting to work on that, making sure that we're moving in the right direction in terms of fulfilling international law and being on the right side of that.

“I think it sort of touched, for me particularly, the refugee story that his family came from and the link that I have for that and how inspiring that can be. It's people from all different cultures and backgrounds, and that's what's really important.

“I think people maybe sort of assume there's only one type of refugee, and as he shows, and Lord Alf Dubs showed previously, refugees come from all different backgrounds, different cultures, and bring so much to this country and improve it and help it be in so many ways, and help build our communities, and I'm so proud that I have that background as well.”

Ms Abdi-Wali is facing off with Green Party leader Zack Polanski in the North London seat, with voters going to the polls this Thursday.

Addressing Ms Braverman’s comments, she said: “I think any this sort of language is really divisive, somewhat hateful, and it can just be really corrosive to the general sort of public conversation we have, and I just don't see the point in it and the need to engage in that.”

“I think as a country, more and more of us are coming together, and it's having that sort of understanding of who we are as a country, the values that we share, and making our country better and our communities better is what really matters.”

News.title: Dr Michael Mosley activity for people who 'can't do conventional exercise' to slash 'silent killer' risk
News.content:
Dr Michael Mosley activity for people who 'can't do conventional exercise' to slash 'silent killer' risk

The late doctor was famous for his easy-to-follow advice and exercises which helped boost the health of numerous people around the world

View Image Dr Michael Mosley suggested three exercises to cut blood pressure which you can do at home

Around one in three adults in the UK has high blood pressure. Known as the 'silent killer', it can lead to strokes, heart attacks, and other health problems.

‌



‌



Under the UK Government’s Cardiovascular Disease Modern Service Framework, cutting high blood pressure is a priority for the NHS. But how can we do that? It may have been more than two years since his passing, but Dr Michael Mosley's legacy lives on. His work in public health touched millions of lives - and he had three simple exercises which could 'help reduce blood pressure in the comfort of your own home'.

‌



What are the exercises?

The Plank

‌



In an Instagram post from SBS Australia, Dr Mosley, who was a GP as well as a TV presenter and documentary maker, is seen demonstrating the three exercises.

"Okay, so this is the plank," he says. "The idea is you go up on your elbows, keep your body straight, and hold this for as long as you can, ideally for up to two minutes, which I can assure you is a long time if you're doing the plank.

"Isometric exercises, where you tighten your muscles but don't actually move them, like the plank or the wall sit, can help reduce blood pressure in the comfort of your own home."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Wall sit

"So, this is the wall sit. You put your legs out about two feet, and this is a real thigh burner. Well, maybe comfort was the wrong word. The idea is you try and hold it for about 20 to 30 seconds, you have a breather, and you go and do it again another couple of times."

‌



Grip strength

"Now, this is a surprising one, and it's particularly suitable if you can't do more conventional exercise. Now, what you have to do is you have to grip this thing, and the idea is you squeeze it, and then you hold it for a couple of minutes. And you do it again a couple more times, and you try and do this about three times a week. You can get hold of these grip strengtheners pretty easily online."

Isometric exercises and blood pressure

As Dr Mosley said, isometric exercises are static muscle contractions where the muscle length and joint angle do not change while you hold a fixed position. One 2023 study from the University of Leicester highlights how effective they are at slashing blood pressure.

‌



The systematic review looked at 270 trials carried out around the world between 1990 and 2023 with almost 16,000 participants. It compared blood pressure readings after doing one of:

Aerobic exercise, such as cycling, walking and jogging

Resistance training, such as lifting weights

Combined training (weights and aerobic exercise)

High-intensity interval training (HIIT), such as sprint intervals

Isometric exercises, such as wall squats

It found that isometric exercises were most effective at cutting blood pressure, followed by combined training, resistance training, aerobic exercise, and HIIT. It also showed that walking was less effective at lowering blood pressure than cycling or running, but wall squats defeated them all when it came to lowering blood pressure.

‌



Wall squats were actually the most effective exercise out of all those compared. Jamie O’Driscoll, a reader in cardiovascular physiology at Canterbury Christ Church university and senior author of the report, said: "They increase the tension in the muscles when held for two minutes, then cause a sudden rush of blood when you relax. This increases the blood flow, but you must remember to breathe."

Why cut blood pressure?

High blood pressure costs the NHS over £2.1 billion every year, according to Public Health England. It is one of the most preventable and treatable health conditions, but half of people with high blood pressure are not diagnosed or receiving treatment.

High blood pressure is responsible for more than half of all strokes and heart attacks, and is also a risk factor for heart disease, kidney disease and vascular dementia.

‌



The NHS says: "If your blood pressure is too high, it puts extra strain on your blood vessels, heart and other organs, such as your brain, kidneys and eyes. If it's not treated, it can increase your risk of serious conditions such as:

Lowering your blood pressure even a small amount can help reduce your risk of these problems. You can lower it by having a healthy, balanced diet, exercising regularly, and losing weight if you are overweight.

Article continues below

Reducing the amount of salt in your diet, cutting back on alcohol and caffeine, and not smoking are also good ways of slashing your blood pressure.

NHS Better Health has free tools and support to help you lose weight, get active, quit smoking, and drink less. There are also lots of different medicines used to lower blood pressure. Which one you are given depends on your age, ethnicity, and how high your blood pressure is. Most are tablets which are taken once a day, although more than one medicine may be needed.

News.title: Locals who helped save cherished village pub to be paid back in pints
News.content:
Locals who helped save cherished village pub to be paid back in pints

Villagers took part in a novel membership scheme to help rescue their closed pub - and can will enjoy being paid back through food, drink and accommodation when it reopens

View 3 Images John Hunter and Annabelle Cochrane, the new owners of the Red Lion pub, hit upon the idea of a membership scheme to allow locals to take part it its rescue (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

A village pub has been saved with the help of locals - who will be paid back in pints.

The Red Lion in Upper Basildon, Berkshire, has stood derelict for nearly three years after closing. As the only hub left in a village, it meant the community was deprived of a place to meet. The building also began to become an eyesore.

Locals launched a bid to buy it from owners the Stonegate Pub Company, but faced the massive task of raising the necessary funds.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

John Hunter and Annabel Cochrane, who run another pub, also called the Red Lion, in nearby Blewbury, heard about the community push and decided to get involved as well. The couple needed to raise £450,000 from residents to help secure the £760,000 purchase, with the difference coming from them.

View 3 Images The Red Lion in Upper Basildon, Berkshire, was facing an uncertain future after closing three years ago (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

They decided to do so through a membership benefit scheme, in which people stumped up either £3,000, £6,000 or £9,000 each, The effort was such a success that they were able to buy the Red Lion late last month, although the work needed to renovate it means the pub is not expected to reopen until next April.

When it does, those who took out either bronze, silver or gold membership will be entitled to loyalty points to the value of either £25, £50 or £75 per month, which they can be exchanged for drinks, food or accommodation.

View 3 Images The inside of the Red Lion pub after it closed (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

The novel idea comes as communities across the country are battling to save beloved pubs that have either closed or are threatened. The Mirror’s Your Pub Needs You campaign has been championing the plight of the nation’s watering holes, highlighting their importance to communities and calling for ways to help those who want to take over at-risk pubs.

Mr Hunter, 68, who used to work as a property developer in London, and Ms Cochrane, 55, were new to running pubs when they bought the Red Lion in Blewbury a few years ago. However, they were keen to use their knowledge to help save the pub in Upper Basildon.

“It was the last chance saloon,” says Mr Hunter, as we recalls the state of the pub. “It was clear that the community was not happy to have a village without a pub. It has no shops, no post office. But after being closed to three years, it was derelict,” he adds, describing it as like the Mary Celeste: “the beer was still in the lines, there were pint glasses and a flat cap on the bar.”

The couple came up with the idea of a membership benefit scheme after mulling idea on how they could potentially open a second pub.

Local support has extended as far as people helping to spruce up the outside of the pub. Community investor Richard Beake helping clear away three years’ worth of overgrown grass, hedges and growth in the beer garden. He told the BBC that buying the pub was as a “milestone” in the village regaining “a vibrant pub”. He also said he was looking forward to drinking pints in the pub as a “return on investment”.

Mr Hunter described the nation’s pubs as “the cornerstone of our culture in this country, of our heritage.”

Article continues below

He said the membership scheme was an idea that could be used by other communities: “It’s a method that could work in a village pub that is the last one. I don’t think it would where there is another pub within walking distance.”

News.title: Kemi Badenoch has cemented her image. Now she wants to put her party back on the big stage
News.content:
The 2026 Conservative conference is big enough to justify using Birmingham's Symphony Hall as its main stage again.

So, Kemi Badenoch will tread the same stage ageing rockers Marillion took last month - and where sequinned soprano Katherine Jenkins will perform next week. She'll also avoid the humiliation of a national party leader being squashed into a side room at a corporate conference centre (with drapes portioning off the empty space). Simply, the party is able to put bums on seats again - and by that measure, things are looking up.

Badenoch goes into the conference with her own position secure in the party. One senior Tory says "she has actually defied cynics like me" who initially disapproved of her leadership. Her standing with the public has improved and she is now, again on a very simple but crucial measure, much better known. Her allies are sure she has developed a clear identity among the public, confiding: "People now know who she is and they enjoy her interventions - the thing we hear most is I don't always agree with her but I know where she stands."

News.title: Homemade bomb part of alleged plot on Manchester's Jewish community, court told
News.content:
Two Iranian men have appeared in court charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb.

Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, were accused at Westminster Magistrates' Court of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September.

One of the buildings they are alleged to have carried out reconnaissance at is the Heaton Park synagogue which was attacked on 2 October 2025.

Both men, who had arrived in the UK by small boat, were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur - the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

Salehi and Ahmadyan were remanded in custody by District Judge Nina Tempia until 23 October, when they will appear at the Old Bailey in London.

As part of the investigation, searches were carried out at addresses in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford.

The Metropolitan Police said the men were alleged to have obtained instructions to make a chlorine bomb, acquired liquids and other components to make an improvised explosive device.

They are accused of using the internet to identify and research potential targets, acquiring images, plans and maps.

Prosecutor Mark Luckett told the court: "Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device.

"The defendants were observed carrying out, what the prosecution say, is a hostile reconnaissance within Manchester's Jewish community, identifying attempted targets such as the Jewish Museum and Heaton Park Synagogue."

News.title: Alison Hammond returns home from hospital after rushing off This Morning
News.content:
"It felt very real to me. I'm really new to panic attacks, so I need to learn more about it," she added.

The Birmingham-born presenter, who also co-hosts The Great British Bake Off, thanked NHS staff and her colleagues at This Morning, including O'Leary.

"It's really warmed my heart actually. I didn't necessarily want to be on the news or anything like that but this is a new world to me," she said.

"I'm going to take stock, take some rest and I'll see you soon."

Friday's edition of the ITV show began at 10:00 BST with Hammond and her regular co-host O'Leary at the helm, before she left at 11:30 during a segment about pets.

O'Leary, 53, addressed her absence when the show returned from a break, saying: "Welcome back to This Morning, Alison is feeling a little unwell, so she's just had to duck out. Hopefully she'll be back."

He later updated viewers that she would, in fact, not be returning, "so I'll be here for the rest of the show".

Hammond rose to fame as contestant on Channel 4 reality show Big Brother before appearing on I'm A Celebrity and Strictly Come Dancing.

She became a co-host in This Morning in 2021, and was part of the team that won a National Television Award for best daytime programme the following year.

She joined Bake Off in 2023 and took over from the late Paul O'Grady on For the Love of Dogs in 2024.

News.title: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises?
News.content:
Months before you have a chance to see your favourite artist, chances are you already know some of the big moments they have planned.

You'll also probably know the set list, the stage design, and - if you've really been paying attention - where to stand to get the best view.

When it comes to films and TV series, spoilers tend to be guarded against with warnings.

But for many major gigs, there's no escaping a stream of fan videos from the shows if you're online, whether you like it or not.

Last week, US pop star Olivia Rodrigo kicked off her Unraveled tour, and surprises from the show, which scores of fans have paid a lot of money to see, have already been dissected online.

Tours by Harry Styles, Charli XCX and Ariana Grande have also been filmed from every angle and shared over the past few months.

While some fans lap up the opportunity to see what's coming, others are taking extreme measures to preserve the element of surprise.

News.title: EV drivers love their cars, but some passengers feel sick - this could be why
News.content:
Lola Baird has just asked her boyfriend to pull over. Forty minutes into a journey and she's feeling "overwhelmed" by nausea - and can't stop herself throwing up on the ground next to his car.

Lola, 24, from north London, had never experienced motion sickness until her boyfriend bought an electric vehicle (EV) two years ago. Ever since, she's been feeling "very nauseous" when he takes her on long car journeys.

It's become so severe she's even asked him to change his car.

Lola isn't alone. Other people told BBC News that they or their children notice feeling more car sick when sitting as a passenger in an electric vehicle. But at the same time, many EV drivers say it's not been a concern.

So what could explain these reports of motion sickness?

Dr Irene Di Giulio, senior lecturer in anatomy and biomechanics at King's College London whose research includes motion sickness, says research so far suggests some people experience more severe motion sickness in electric vehicles than in non-electric vehicles.

It's something Dr Nicholas Hac, a neurologist at Northwestern Medicine in Chicago who specialises in dizziness and vertigo, has also heard from some of his patients. "They just notice that they're much more likely or prone to be motion sick" in electric vehicles, he says.

"I've heard about it many, many, many times," he adds, saying about two patients a month specifically reference feeling motion sick in electric vehicles.

News.title: Traitors claim their first victim as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.

As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.

Unfortunately, it fell to Amol Rajan to become the Paloma Faith of this series - being taken away in a coffin in episode two before even having the chance to take part in a banishment.

"It's gutting to be the first out," Rajan said afterwards, noting that perhaps it was because he had been "a bit bullish with Richard" earlier in the day.

"But you know what, games are games, and just as there are winners, so there have to be losers."

The episode drew in a peak audience of 8.6 million viewers, just short of the debut episode with an average of 8.9 million viewers.

The morning following Rajan's banishment, presenter Claudia Winkleman confirmed the University Challenge host's murder to the other players, joking: "That's what I call a starter for 10."

Acaster, meanwhile, reflected: "I'm gutted to not be a faithful anymore, I don't like lying. But if I don't join them, they'll kill me." You can't fault his logic.

The decision meant that Grant, an Oscar-nominated actor with a Razzie-worthy traitor strategy, did at least manage to commit one successful murder despite his shambolic first day.

News.title: Why thousands of couples are choosing Scotland to say 'I do'
News.content:
Hayden Kuhn and Savannah Aanderud had never set foot in Scotland before they decided it was the perfect place to get married last May.

The couple, from Pennsylvania in the US, wanted a destination wedding that would take their family and friends on an adventure with them.

They considered locations across Europe, before deciding on Scotland after Savannah saw photographs of a castle wedding online.

"I think it was on Pinterest," she said. "Somebody got married in a castle and I was like 'Oh, I have to do that'."

The pair are far from alone in seeing Scotland as the ultimate romantic destination.

News.content:

News.title: Greens would offer two-year jobs to unemployed under-24s
News.content:
Young people would be offered a guaranteed two-year job within four months of leaving education or training, under a new proposal unveiled by the Green Party.

Announcing the policy at the party's conference in Brighton, co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said there were a million "bored, desperate and lost" young people who were out of work, training or education.

Under the proposed scheme, youngsters would be offered posts in the private sector, with the government paying half their salary.

The Greens have not specified a budget for the policy, but have argued it would reduce spending on welfare and boost tax receipts from employment.

The party says it would initially target the plan in areas with the fewest jobs openings for young people, citing Rotherham, Ceredigion, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Broxtowe and South Staffordshire, with an ambition to roll it out nationwide.

Employers would be exempt from paying National Insurance contributions, but would have to provide in-job training, the party says.

The party is seeking to pitch the plan as more ambitious than the government's own scheme, which subsidises six-month job placements for benefit claimants who have been looking for work for 18 months.

Ali also criticised ministers for previously suggesting youngsters refusing a role under that scheme could lose access to benefits, telling activists: "Threatening young people with cuts to Universal Credit if they don't accept short-term work placements - that's not a youth strategy."

He added: "Working class kids should be able to dream. But more than dream, they should have a genuine chance of making those dreams a reality.

The number of 16-24-year-olds who are not in employment, education or training has been rising since the Covid pandemic, with figures reaching almost one million.

A long-awaited report into the problem by former Labour minister Alan Milburn is expected to be published this autumn.

News.title: Suppliers pile pressure on government over energy bills
News.content:
The government should take immediate action to help those struggling with energy bills this winter, the suppliers' trade body has said.

Energy UK said domestic gas prices, which rose on Thursday, and forecasts of steep rises in January meant inaction would lead to a longer-term, more costly and deeper crisis.

Figures revealed by the BBC earlier this week showed forecasters predicting a 16% rise in domestic energy prices in the new year for 20 million households on variable tariffs affected by regulator Ofgem's price cap.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the government was considering any measure that took the pressure off.

Households in England, Scotland and Wales on variable energy tariffs set by Ofgem's price cap, which puts a maximum price on each unit of gas and electricity, were hit with a 4% price increase at the start of October.

That is the equivalent of about Â£60 per year - or Â£5 per month - taking an annual bill to Â£1,723 for the typical household using both electricity and gas and paying by direct debit if this level was sustained for a year.

But forecasts show a far greater increase is possible for bills in January. Consultancy Cornwall Insight said its latest forecast suggested the same typical annual bill would rise to Â£1,999.

News.title: Tories pledge to build 50,000 new prison places
News.content:
The Conservatives have promised to build 50,000 new prison places in England and Wales to stop criminals being released early, if they return to government.

The party said it would cost Â£2bn per year to build and run the new prisons, funded by spending cuts including to the foreign aid budget.

On Thursday hundreds of prisoners were released early, under new rules introduced to prevent jails reaching capacity, with around 4,500 due to be freed by next summer.

Labour blamed the previous Tory government for leaving "our criminal justice system at breaking point" and said the party's proposals were not "credible".

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham, which begins on Sunday.

Prisons in England and Wales have been running close to capacity for years, with the latest government figures showing they are 98% full.

Under the latest early release scheme, eligible prisoners can now be released on a community licence after serving one-third of their jail sentence.

Those excluded include prisoners convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death.

The government has also effectively scrapped one-year jail terms.

The Tories said they would use extra prison capacity to reverse these measures.

An early release programme introduced by the previous Conservative government saw more than 10,000 prisoners freed early between October 2023 and September 2024.

News.title: Teenager taken to hospital after Glasgow shopping centre gang attack
News.content:
A teenager who was attacked by a gang of youths inside a Glasgow shopping centre has been treated in hospital for his injuries.

Video posted on social media shows the young man, who was using a crutch and wearing a medical boot, being knocked to the ground, then repeatedly punched and kicked inside the St Enoch Centre on Friday afternoon.

A second person was also pushed to the ground but security staff intervened.

Police Scotland said the 19-year-old was taken to hospital and officers were reviewing CCTV footage to identify his assailants.

The attackers had run off by the time officers arrived and the injured man, who was bleeding from a head wound, was initially helped by shoppers and security staff.

News.title: Police searching for mum of baby girl found on shoreline tell her not to be afraid to call
News.content:
Police searching for the mother of a newborn baby girl whose body was found on a north Wales shoreline have set up a special phone line, urging her to contact them.

A member of the public found the body on the Menai Strait shoreline near Siliwen Road in Bangor, Gwynedd, on Sunday shortly before 17:00 BST.

In an update on Thursday, North Wales Police said a post-mortem examination revealed the newborn was a girl, adding that she may have been in the water for up to a few weeks.

Supt Llinos Davies from North Wales Police said a specialist would take a call from the woman directly and could support her confidentially and told the woman not to be afraid to speak to the police.

"We understand that you may be scared to come forward, but we urge you to contact us," Davies said.

"I want to reassure you that your welfare and safety continues to be our priority and utmost concern and that you receive any medical attention and support you may need.

"Whatever has happened, you do not have to face this on your own," she added.

The director of midwifery and women's services for Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board Fiona Giraud last week also appealed directly to the mother to come forward.

News.title: Derelict 'church in the woods' sold at auction
News.content:
A derelict Grade II listed church located in a wooded area of Leeds has been sold at auction.

St Mary's In The Wood United Reformed Church on Commercial Street in Morley sold for Â£100,000 earlier this week, auctioneers BTG Eddisons confirmed.

The 19th Century building has not been used for worship since 2008 and fell into disrepair after sustaining extensive fire damage two years later.

A previous planning application lodged with Leeds City Council which has since lapsed proposed the site could be repurposed into a hotel, restaurant and car park.

Later plans to transform the fire-damaged church into 18 apartments also did not come to fruition.

The fire started about 02:30 BST in June 2010 and caused 20 people living nearby to be evacuated to a nearby supermarket due to fears the church steeple could collapse.

In 2023, Leeds City Council purchased the nearby former Sunday School building, which was built in 1900, for use as a "learning and skills centre".

However, the older, Gothic revival-style building, built in 1878, has remained vacant for more than 15 years.

BTG Eddisons could not disclose whether St Mary's was bought by a commercial or private buyer.

News.title: Trains cancelled after bedbugs found on board
News.content:
A number of train services were cancelled after drivers discovered bedbugs in their cabs.

Carriages on two affected trains were locked to isolate passenger areas from the cabs, said Southeastern, which operates services in Kent, East Sussex and Greater London.

The rail firm said the trains only remained in service while they "returned to a suitable location for inspection and if necessary, treatment".

The cancellations took place on mainline routes after the bugs were spotted on 22 September. None of the insects were found on any High Speed 1 trains, it added.

In a social media post, Southeastern said the affected trains were based at the West Marina Depot in Hastings, the terminus point for trains from London.

Services on the route go via Battle, Tunbridge Wells and Sevenoaks.

A spokesperson for the firm said trains and stations are cleaned "thoroughly" so passengers can "travel safely and with confidence".

Oly Turner, head of drivers at Southeastern, said: "We have a great relationship with our drivers, who have helped hugely in cooperating with us over these isolated incidents.

"When we receive reports such as these we check trains thoroughly before they are put back into service when given the all clear.

"Cases have been contained to the drivers' cabs in only two of our trains and no bed bugs have been identified in areas for passengers."

News.title: Victorian bridge hidden under reservoir is revealed
News.content:
The former Bessom Bridge used to cross a stream that fed into the River Haddeo, while the new one crosses the north side of the lake.

When water levels drop, the old bridge can be seen from the new one.

Shipley said the changing landscape on Exmoor was "extraordinary".

"The photographs are incredible, they're just so dramatic of the bridge poking out from the silt and sediment that's covered it.

"We live in an ever-changing world and it's not a kind of fixed point where things stay the same, but then by contrastâ¦ there's been a consistency of settlement and people living in farming and working in similar ways, so it's that balance of understanding how the world around us is always changing and responding, but also recognising that some things are really consistent over time."

She added that the historic bridge could be enjoyed from afar and asked visitors to refrain from walking on the dried-up section of the reservoir.

Elsewhere around the county, traces of centuries-old gardens were found in Bishop's Palace in Wells, while relics of old structures were uncovered at Glastonbury Abbey due to the record-breaking summer temperatures.

David Beckham has said he "couldn’t be prouder" of Lady Victoria Beckham following her latest show at Paris Fashion Week.

The designer's fashion brand showcased its new collection on Friday evening at the Conciergerie at 2 Boulevard du Palais, accompanied by key members of the Beckham family in attendance.

Following the event, the retired footballer praised his wife's craftsmanship and dedication.

He wrote: "We are so proud of you, yet again you show your elegance, passion & beauty in how you want people to feel in your clothes.

"We feel so lucky to be part of your beautiful night in a place that we love so much . Well done we couldn’t be prouder."

The 51-year-old uploaded a photograph posing alongside his wife, alongside a family shot featuring their children Romeo, 24, Cruz, 21, and Harper, 15.

Kim Turnbull and Jackie Apostel, who are dating his sons, also joined the family group image.

Once the presentation concluded, Lady Victoria shared the identical snapshot on Instagram alongside images of several attending guests.

"To my friends and family, I feel so blessed to have you all by my side xxx," she wrote.

Commenting on her upload, Sir David added: "We are all so proud of you as always. Pure elegance, grace & beauty, what a beauty show. We love you."

Sharing a clip of models on the runway, Cruz tagged his mother and posted: "Killed it as always."

Noticeably absent were the couple's eldest son Brooklyn, 27, and his wife Nicola Peltz Beckham, 31, who did not attend despite being present in Paris.

In January, Brooklyn released a statement on social media claiming his parents were "controlling" him and "trying to ruin" his relationship with his wife.

While staying in the French capital, the pair chose instead to attend other fashion shows, including Balenciaga and Messika.

Models walk the runway during the Victoria Beckham Womenswear Spring/Summer 2027 show as part of Paris Fashion Week ( Getty )

In August, it was disclosed that the label had achieved an operating profit for the first time in its 18-year history.

Founded in 2008 prior to a ready-to-wear debut at New York Fashion Week, the company faced debts approaching £54 million by 2022.

However, the Financial Times revealed two months ago that filings for Victoria Beckham Holdings Ltd showed an operating profit of £7.3 million for 2025, reversing a £1.6 million loss from the prior year.

Total revenues for the business increased by 15% to reach £129.8 million in 2025, compared with £112.7 million in 2024.

Discussing the financial progress, Lady Beckham said: "We have all worked hard for a long time for this moment of profitability and growth.

"We’ve been very transparent about the problems that we had in the business but have recovered and are now growing at a sensible pace.

"After 20 years, people don’t look at my brand as a celebrity brand anymore."

News.title: Alison Hammond gives ‘very real’ update after shock health scare
News.content:
Alison Hammond has confirmed she is “home and safe” after suffering what turned out to be a panic attack during a live broadcast of This Morning on Friday (2 October).

The presenter, 51, had been rushed for medical attention after experiencing heart palpitations on camera, leaving co-host Dermot O'Leary to continue the show alone.

Following checks on her heart, lungs and blood at the NHS, all results came back clear. Addressing fans on social media, Hammond said: "It felt very real to me. I'm really new to panic attacks, so I need to learn more about it."
