Sports.title: Verstappen beats Hamilton to pole in Malaysia
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first pole position of the season as he beat Lewis Hamilton in qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Verstappen and Hamilton will share the front row in Sunday's race at 8am (build-up from 6.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event, for the first time since Hungary 2023 after the Red Bull driver delivered a dominant qualifying performance.

The Dutchman topped each segment of qualifying and set two laps good enough for pole, ending up 0.298s faster than Hamilton who will target a second Ferrari win of the season.

"Verstappen versus Hamilton. Imagine that! What could possibly go wrong..." reacted Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar equalled his best career qualifying result with third but will start eighth due to a five-grid place penalty for a new internal combustion engine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player SkyPad analysis of how Max Verstappen claimed first pole in 2026

Mercedes were surprisingly unable to challenge Verstappen for pole despite bringing their first major upgrade package since May's Canadian Grand Prix to this weekend's race in Malaysia.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start third after a costly mistake in Q2 forced him to use an extra set of tyres prior to Q3, leaving him with just one run in the final part of qualifying.

Antonelli is 66 points ahead of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the Drivers' Championship and, crucially, Russell will start seventh as he lacked pace throughout Saturday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff explains Mercedes issues after big upgrade package at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc will be fourth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri who were never in contention for pole.

Alpine's Pierre Gasly was the fastest driver outside of F1's top four teams in ninth from Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto in 10th.

Aston Martin enjoyed their best qualifying since the summer break as Fernando Alonso claimed 12th and Lance Stroll 14th.

Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad gave team-mate Liam Lawson a slipstream in Q2, as the British driver will start at the back of the grid for changing his power unit, but Lawson just missed out and will start 11th.

Bahrain GP Qualifying: Top 10 1) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



2) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



3) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull*



4) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



5) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



6) Lando Norris, McLaren



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) George Russell, Mercedes



9) Pierre Gasly, Alpine



10) Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi



*5-place grid penalty to be applied

Dominant Verstappen as Mercedes left confused

Red Bull impressed on Friday's two practice sessions but Mercedes looked to have made big gains overnight as Antonelli topped final practice by nearly three tenths from Verstappen.

But, come qualifying, Verstappen looked untouchable as qualifying progressed with a few tenths of an advantage over the field which was proven in Q3.

Verstappen won the last F1 race in Malaysia in 2017 and was in a league of his own as he took provisional pole from team-mate Hadjar after the first runs by three tenths with the Ferraris and McLarens in behind.

Hamilton produced a great lap to get onto the front row but he was unable to knock Verstappen off top spot and the four-time world champion made sure of pole by improving even more on his final Q3 run.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the thrilling end to qualifying at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia!

"It's fantastic. We have been trying many Grands Prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible," said Verstappen.

"I'm happy with today and, for sure, I'm going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that's the target."

Having won the last three races, and with big upgrades on their car, Mercedes came into Malaysia as big favourites to even dominate the race weekend.

But the extremely abrasive track surface and high track temperatures have thrown a spanner in the works and Mercedes appear to be hurt most by those factors.

"It's a very demanding circuit on the tyres, the tarmac is all broke up, it's extremely rough, it's so hot out there and the tyres are going through hell," Russell told Sky Sports F1.

"For whatever reason, it seems to be affecting us far more than others."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell and Kimi Antonelli react to Mercedes' qualifying at Bahrain GP in Malaysia

Antonelli may have been closer to pole if not for a track limits excursion in Q2 which saw his lap deleted, and Mercedes elected to put another new set of softs on his car to ensure he reached Q3.

However, that left Antonelli with only one new set of softs and, with the tyres only holding up well for one lap, the Italian was not right on the limit but still qualified fourth behind the penalised Hadjar and half a second behind pole-sitter Verstappen.

Russell won last time out in Baku and said his "confidence is back" but Malaysia was always going to be the big final test due to its track characteristics of wide, medium-speed corners where Antonelli has generally been quicker this year.

The British driver was unable to unlock the same pace as Antonelli in final practice and qualifying, so faces an uphill battle on Sunday to gain some serious title momentum over his team-mate.

Sports.title: Antonelli fastest from Verstappen ahead of qualifying in Malaysia
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli was fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to set up a Mercedes versus Red Bull fight for pole position.

Antonelli, who leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, struggled on Friday but was 0.278s quicker than Verstappen.

Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar took third ahead of Russell fourth but both drivers were more than half a second behind Antonelli, who appears to have found a nice rhythm in time for qualifying later on Saturday at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1, at the Sepang International Circuit.

Mercedes have brought their biggest upgrade package since May's Canadian Grand Prix to Malaysia but Red Bull look set to be a threat again, just as they were last time out in Baku.

"Red Bull would have hoped to be closer to the Mercedes, but they are there or thereabouts once again," said Sky Sports F1's Anthony Davidson.

"They're quickly becoming the team that's the biggest threat to Mercedes on any given weekend."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Bernie Collins takes a look at Mercedes upgrades as they head into the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc topped second practice but was seven tenths back in fifth while his team-mate Lewis Hamilton was sixth, despite providing positive feedback following his final practice lap.

McLaren appeared to be out of contention for pole as Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri were seventh and eighth, although the fact Norris' best lap was done on the mediums suggested they retain room for improvement.

Tyres are a major talking point this weekend due to the extremely rough track surface coupled with the high temperatures and humidity as F1 races in Malaysia for the first time since 2017, with the country having stepped in to host for Bahrain following the original race being postponed earlier this year due to insecurity in the Persian Gulf.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell said on Friday that the track conditions were trumping Mercedes' upgrades on the Sepang International Circuit

Alpine's Franco Colapinto, who has a combined 15-grid place penalty for causing a collision last weekend in Baku and taking a new engine in Sepang, was ninth in final practice and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad was 10th.

There was a brief red flag after a piece of debris got stuck on Oliver Bearman's Haas after falling onto the circuit at Turn 10, seeing the session momentarily stopped to allow for a marshal to collect it.

Fernando Alonso continued his strong weekend for Aston Martin in 12th and Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto was 11th, so at least four teams are in the battle for the final points-paying positions.

Sports.title: Scandinavia seeks sixth Group 1 in Prix du Cadran
Sports.content:
Scandinavia takes on Queenstown and Caballo De Mar as Arc weekend gets underway - live on Sky Sports Racing.

4.00 ParisLongchamp - Star stayer Scandinavia bids for a sixth Group 1 success

Superstar stayer Scandinavia is the headline act on Day 1 of the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe meeting. Aidan O'Brien's prolific winner heads a field of 10 for this Prix du Cadran.

He arrives unbeaten in his past eight starts recording a staggering five Group 1 wins in the process and looks hard to oppose as he heads up in distance once again.

Stablemate Queenstown, the ride of Wayne Lordan, heads the likely dangers. He returned with an excellent victory in Group 3 company at the Curragh in August before chasing home Scandinavia in the Irish St Leger. Third in this race last year, he could hit the frame once more.

George Scott's defending champion Caballo De Mar cannot be ruled out after bouncing back to form with a comfortable success in the Doncaster Cup, while Double Major is the pick of the bigger prices.

3.25 ParisLongchamp - Top fillies Sunly and Waardah lock horns

Classy pair Sunly and Wardaah headline a field of 11 for this Group 1 Prix de Royallieu.

Francis-Henri Graffard skipped the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe in favour of this contest and his charge Sunly will be a short price to land a maiden top-level success under Christophe Soumillon. She could outclass her rivals if staying this extra yardage.

Wardaah took the Park Hill Stakes at Doncaster on her last start, beating Consent and Cameo in the process and looks ready for a crack at this better grade.

Image: Waardah tasted success at Doncaster's St Leger meeting

Consent saw off Santorini Star to land this race last season and, after finishing fourth at Goodwood and third at Doncaster, she seems to be progressing with each outing.

Ribblesdale winner Earth Shot is another who makes each-way appeal in a stellar field.

3.35 Ascot - Thunder Call and Mezcala headline 18 runners

A typically competitive edition of the BetMGM Challenge Cup where Thunder Call and Mezcala will be fancied in a field of 18.

The William Haggas-trained Thunder Call handled the step up to seven furlongs when easily disposing of a good field over this course and distance last month and should have more to give despite a tricky draw in stall one.

Jack Channon saddles Mezcala, who landed the Buckingham Palace Stakes over this trip and track at the Royal meeting and has been dropped 1lb for his latest sixth at Doncaster.

Several have place chances including course specialist Hickory, while George Boughey's Moonfall took the Britannia here, caught the eye at Doncaster last time, but must prove he can handle to dip to seven furlongs.

Also at ParisLongchamp...

Having faltered in the St Leger last time out, Pierre Bonnard will be looking to bonce back when he goes to post for the Group 2 Prix Chaudenay at 12.23pm. The son of Camelot was only beaten two lengths by Arc hopeful Maltese Cross in the Great Voltigeur and looks the class act of the field. In opposition, Space Waltz represents the formidable Fabre team while Amy Murphy saddles the hat-trick-seeking Victoire Magique.

Image: Pierre Bonnard returns on Saturday afternoon

Wimbledon Hawkeye and Phineas clash in the subsequent Group 2 Prix Dollar, with the former horse arguably unlucky to have been denied in the Irish Champion Stakes last time. Phineas has won four on the spin and looks to be a real talent for the Fabre operation, while Distant Storm represents Charlie Appleby and Godolphin once more after success at Deauville last time.

Quddwah tops the runners assembled for the 4.35pm Prix Daniel Wildenstein, while Fallen Angel and 2025 Sussex Stakes winner Qirat line up to take him on.

Domestically...

The John and Thady Gosden-trained So Regal looks the pick of the runners declared for Ascot's 1.15pm BetMGM British EBF October Stakes, having ran with credit in Group 3 company when last seen. Of the others, three-time winner Secret History could be the chief threat, despite not running to her optimum level in a competitive York handicap in August.

Tuco Salamanca and Regional lock horns in the five-furlong BetMGM Rous Stakes (1.50pm) before crowd favourite Al Aasy faces five rivals in the BetMGM Cumberland Lodge Stakes (2.25pm). A hardy individual, he showed real tenacity to defeat Chestnut Rocket - who lines up in Sunday's Arc - at Deauville when last seen.

It's Prince Of India versus Division in the 3pm John Guest Racing Bengough Stakes, with the latter favourite in the market after being narrowly beaten by Samangan in France recently.

Fontwell and Southwell open their gates for action over jumps and on the Flat, with 15 races scheduled between them.

Internationally...

The day begins with three Group 1 contests from Australia, with Sir Delius and Aeliana involved in Flemington's 7.25am Turnball Stakes after top clashes from Randwick earlier in the morning.

A Grade 2 runner-up earlier in the campaign, Francis-Henri Graffard's Mandanaba eyes a return to the winners' enclosure when she contests the 9.44pm First Lady Stakes. Classic Q is partnered with John Velazquez for this step up to Grade 1 company here, while stablemate And One More Time seeks a hat-trick for Mark Casse.

American History looked to have the makings of a real star when bolting up on debut by eight lengths. Todd Pletcher's charge returns to action in the Claiborne Breeders' Futurity - a Grade 1 for two-year-olds.

Purview takes on Ancient Egypt in the Grade 1 Canadian International from Woodbine before attention switches back to the United States and Keeneland's Coolmore Turf Mile. Lake Forest flies the flag for the Haggas stable in here, with Cieren Fallon booked to ride.

Sports.title: Manchester City whistleblower ready to help UK authorities in return for protection
Sports.content:
Rui Pinto, whose leaks helped to trigger the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs, is prepared to help authorities in the UK with their legal case in exchange for protection from threats, the Guardian understands.

Despite the crowdfunding campaign launched on Friday to fund a new life after leaving the protection of the Portuguese police, the whistleblower’s priority remains to cooperate, provided adequate security arrangements are in place.

In addition to the sporting ramifications of the case being conducted against City by the Premier League, British authorities could also decide to extend the inquiry. That has already occurred in Portugal in relation to some of the documents disclosed by Pinto. City were found guilty of more than 100 charges by an independent commission that unearthed “sham” contracts to boost income artificially by £900m, an investigation that was prompted by Pinto’s leaks of thousands of private documents.

City confirmed on Friday the club will appeal against the tribunal’s verdict.

With detailed knowledge of the documents, individuals and companies involved in the case – as well as documents that may have been overlooked during the investigation – Rui Pinto is willing to continue as a protected witness in another country, it is understood.

Just days before his arrest in Budapest in January 2019, the 37-year-old Portuguese national was negotiating entry into a witness protection programme in France, an initiative that was halted by the Portuguese authorities.

If it is confirmed that Rui Pinto will no longer be a protected witness in Portugal, he will be free to cooperate with authorities in other countries from 10 October. He has cooperated sporadically with French, German and Belgian authorities. The UK could now be added to that list, should it wish to do so.

Pinto’s potential contribution in the UK could extend well beyond the City furore. The hundreds of millions of files he gathered as part of Football Leaks and Luanda Leaks are not solely in the possession of the Portuguese authorities.

Between his arrest in Hungary and his extradition to Portugal, French authorities travelled to the Hungarian capital and copied the contents of all the electronic devices in the whistleblower’s possession. Rui Pinto was later acquitted of 241 counts after a second trial in Portugal in April this year.

The documents can now be shared between countries as part of international cooperation between nations with bilateral ties, including the UK.

Rui Pinto is now waiting to find out what his future holds. His defence protested against the decision of ending the protection, accusing Portugal of “state terrorism”. The whistleblower’s lawyers said they had appealed against the decision and had sought to establish how the risk assessment had been carried out but had received no response.

The hacker says he wants to leave Portugal for a secret location. At the time of writing, more than €19,000 (£16,530) had already been raised by a crowdfunding campaign.

45m ago 08.45 EDT The Turkish Football Federation is working to shake up its refereeing oversight body after its top official was jailed pending trial on graft charges, report AFP. Ferhat Gundogdu, who heads the Central Referees Committee (MHK), and six other referee officials appeared in court Friday on suspicion of manipulating the referee administration process. The judge placed Gundogdu and four others in pre-trial detention, while granting the two other officials conditional release. “In light of these developments, work is ongoing to form a new Central Referees Committee,” the TFF said in a statement on its website, its first comment on the arrests, which happened on Tuesday. The seven accused face charges that include “official document forgery”, “breach of trust” and “illegal acquisition of personal data”. The scandal came exactly a year after the TFF suspended 149 referees on charges of illegal betting. Share

50m ago 08.40 EDT Marc Cucurella, speaking at the Spain press conference, on the subject of the Ballon D’or: “If I had to vote for myself, I would vote for myself.” Spain play Czechia later tonight. Share

1h ago 08.29 EDT More detail on that stormy Ireland press conference via the Press Association: “There was a request from the Irish press officer to keep the line of inquiry to “football questions”, and Hallgrimsson took a question about Finn Azaz’s availability. “A different Israeli journalist said “your players called our players monkeys” – an accusation the Irish press officer said was “completely untrue”, before he ended the press conference as shouting continued. “FAI representatives requested the Israel press leave a subsequent embargoed media opportunity with Hallgrimsson – intended for Irish press only – in a seating area outside the room, sparking another confrontation. A solution was eventually found to hold the briefing elsewhere in the building.” Share

1h ago 08.03 EDT UAE may halt UK investments after Manchester City guilty verdict This story is opening up way beyond mere football governance. double quotation mark Emirati officials said “the Premier League’s actions” would “have an influence on the bilateral state relationship”, according to Bloomberg. Elsewhere, the Telegraph said the UAE is threatening to withdraw a multi-billion pound investment into a Silicon Valley-style Oxbridge tech hub. The Premier League brought 115 charges against Man City for breaches of financial rules between 2009 and 2018. Of those charges, 114 were upheld by an independent commission in September, which described City’s activities as a “sham” multiple times, adding that their witnesses used at the hearing were “dishonest.” UAE may halt UK investments after Manchester City guilty verdict Read more Share

2h ago 07.50 EDT The FAI is continuing to investigate allegations that Irish players Adam Idah and James Abankwah were racially abused in Sunday’s 3-0 win over the Israelis in Hungary. “It just goes to a ⁠process both in our departments and then UEFA to look at,” Hallgrimsson said. “I think it ​was something that was reported from both ​teams. I just hope that we can ​focus on football and that football will be the winner after this. “I think all the challenges that this team has gone through, all the criticism, yeah, I think just surviving as a group after this game, that will be a big win for me and for this group, (and) for the (football) association.” Share

2h ago 07.47 EDT Last week’s Republic of Ireland v Israel game was a stormy affair, both pre-match and post-match. The calmest bit was the game being played, where Ireland won 3-0 very easily. They meet again on Sunday in Serbia and the preliminaries have again been stormy. Via the Irish Independent’s Dan McDonnell on X: “Ireland press conference in Serbia cut short after FAI shut down questions from Israeli media related to the flydubai hijack and then a racism allegation directed at an Irish player which has been strongly refuted by the FAI. Some angry scenes in the room and afterwards.” And the Irish Times’ Gavin Cooney: “Chaotic scenes at Ireland press conference. An Israeli journalist makes an allegation against Irish players which FAI press officer rejects, cutting short the press conference. Led to angry verbal confrontations within the room and again outside...as the FAI attempted to continue with an interview of Hallgrimsson for the Irish media present. It was eventually concluded elsewhere in the stadium.” Quote from Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Ireland coach: “Surviving this camp and coming out of this together would be a massive win for me. That is coming from my heart.” Share

2h ago 07.27 EDT Some Opta stats ahead of Croatia v England at 5pm (BST). Since beating England in the 2018 World Cup semi-final, Croatia are winless in all four of their meetings with the Three Lions (D1 L3), including two Nations League fixtures in 2018 (0-0 home, 1-2 away).



England have won five of their last seven matches against Croatia in all competitions (D1 L1), dating back to the 3-2 defeat in 2007 that cost them qualification for Euro 2008.



The Three Lions have scored at least four goals in three of those wins, triumphing 4-1 in September 2008, 5-1 in September 2009 and 4-2 in their opening group stage clash at the 2026 FIFA World Cup four months ago.



England have won their last eight away games in all competitions, and another victory would see them match their all-time record, set under Sir Alf Ramsey in 1967. Share

Despite all the moaning about missed opportunities and style, I still think finishing third in a World Cup in the Americas was a pretty fine effort by Thomas Tuchel and his squad. I think we’re all still close to it and obsessed by the detail to appreciate the actual bottom line. Perhaps it just needs time. Anyway, ahead of this evening’s Croatia v England clash, here’s David Hytner’s match report from that 4-2 win for the Three Lions in Dallas. England surge to thrilling opening win in World Cup cracker with Croatia Read more Share

2h ago 07.03 EDT Michael O’Neill was delighted with his young Northern Ireland side after they stunned Ukraine 3-0 in Slovakia to move clear at the top of Nations League Group B2. Ciaron Brown scored his first two international goals either side of Isaac Price’s first-half header as Northern Ireland delivered a complete performance which can be another key marker in the development of this team. Besides the 28-year-old Brown every player who started was 24 or younger, with this Northern Ireland’s youngest post-war starting eleven with an average age of just 22. But they showed no fear playing away to a side ranked 37 places ahead of them in the world as they made it back-to-back away wins in this group, still yet to concede after their opening three matches. Brown prodded in his first nine minutes in and, after Price headed in a cross from teenager Kieran Morrison, got his second in bizarre fashion just after the hour as Ukraine goalkeeper Dmytro Riznyk let an intended flick on through his legs. “It’s a great result for us, a great performance,” O’Neill said. “The early goal helps settle us into the game. “The second goal was a brilliant goal. We worked it the length of the pitch. We were patient. We could have crossed it early but that allowed us to get more men in the box and it’s a brilliant header from Isaac. “The third goal is fortuitous but it’s a mistake by the opposition so we have to capitalise on that, but I thought throughout our performance was brilliant. We limited the opposition to crosses and shots from outside the box and I thought we defended brilliantly.” (PA Media) Share

6h ago 03.59 EDT Croatia v England 'behind closed doors' … but mainly full Despite the belief that Croatia v England is being played behind closed doors, that isn’t quite the case. The match in Rijeka officially has that status due to a Uefa punishment for Croatia following crowd trouble involving their supporters during a Nations League quarter-final against France. However, Uefa’s disciplinary rules include an exception for children up to the age of 14 from schools and/or football academies in the local Rijeka area, who have been invited to the match free of charge. Uefa had initially anticipated around 3,000 children plus guardians, but the Croatian federation now expects between 5,500 and 6,000. In an 8,200-seat stadium, that puts it somewhere around 70% full. Add in the 100 England fans allowed to attend and there will be more atmosphere than expected. Perhaps very high-pitched, screechy atmosphere but surely that’s better than eerie silence. Possibly.
