Sports.title: John Fury hits out at brother Peter, calling him a 'cockroach' for joining Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of Cardiff showdown
Sports.content:
John Fury called out his brother Peter for being a 'cockroach' after his estranged brother joined Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of the Briton's showdown with his son Tyson in December.

The long-awaited Battle of Britain is set to take place in Cardiff after months of back-and-forth between the Fury and Joshua camps, but neither John nor Peter will be in the corner of the Gypsy King, after Joshua announced this week that Fury's uncle had helped with his preparations.

Eyebrows were raised due to Peter's family ties, but Fury shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years.

His father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives.'

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

John Fury called out his brother Peter (left) for potentially helping Tyson's rival Anthony Joshua ahead of their Cardiff showdown (pictured in 2015)

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

John may have been staunchly defensive of Fury in the context of Peter doing anything to sabotage him in the ring, but relations between father and son remain minimal after having been, in John's words, 'completely destroyed'.

The duo are at loggerheads over Fury Junior's career, with his father adamant that he should prioritise his health and wellbeing by retiring for good after two failed attempts.

Peter previously trained Fury between 2011 and 2017, but left the camp amid a schism with father and son.

The Gypsy King had previously sought to set the record straight on Peter's involvement with his rival on social media, deeming Joshua's comments 'categorically untrue'.

'Even if Peter Fury hated me, he’s still my family,' he said. 'That would mean he would be a Fredo, scorpion, snake, rat, b****** piece of s*** if he did that.'

Sports.title: Inside Jamie and Rebekah Vardy's new life... at Burnley! Why family made abrupt return from Italy, why striker chose unfashionable new club and how he's taking on Gary Neville and Gary Lineker
Sports.content:
Inside Jamie and Rebekah Vardy's new life... at Burnley! Why family made abrupt return from Italy, why striker chose unfashionable new club and how he's taking on Gary Neville and Gary Lineker

It's now been a month since Jamie Vardy opted to return to English football with Burnley, following his year-long rollercoaster of an adventure with Italian minnows Cremonese.

The 39-year-old did have the option to continue his stay in the quaint city of Cremona, but after the club’s relegation back to Serie B, he made the decision at the end of last season to move on.

Vardy, his wife Rebekah and their children moved back home almost immediately after his contract came to an end, with the striker’s future in football still uncertain.

The former England international took his time to decide his next step before, at the beginning of September, agreeing to move to a struggling Burnley side who were - and still are - bottom of the Championship.

The Lancashire club are winless following relegation from the Premier League last season, picking up just the one point from the two games Vardy has featured in. The veteran has only made cameos off the bench so far.

The big question posed by many since the move was confirmed is: why did Vardy choose Burnley?

Jamie Vardy switched Cremonese in Italy for Championship side Burnley this summer

Why trade the beautiful Lake Garda, where his family’s £2million mansion was surrounded by the scenery of the stunning Gardesane Prealps and deep blue water, for the industrial town of Burnley?

It may seem like a confusing choice to your average Joe who dreams of a life of luxury such as the one the Vardys were living on the Italian lakes - but for Jamie and Rebekah, the decision to return to England was more straightforward.

Daily Mail Sport understands that from a family perspective, they felt they rushed their decision to uproot their life and make the move to Cremonese in 2025.

While they enjoyed the experience in many ways, they had issues living away from home, as showcased in their three-part reality documentary series on ITV, The Vardys.

The move, which they originally thought might last two seasons, was far from plain sailing not just for the parents, but for their four children as well.

Homesickness swept the Vardys' lavish Italian apartment, and things were made worse when it was raided by burglars, leaving Rebekah 'on edge 24/7'.

‘The biggest challenge was trying to balance the excitement of a completely new adventure with the emotional reality of leaving behind a life we'd built over more than a decade,’ Rebekah said in the documentary.

‘Leicester was home for us in every sense - our friends, routines, schools, memories, so uprooting wasn't just about packing boxes and moving country, it was about starting again emotionally.

The 39-year-old had been living by beautiful Lake Garda while playing in Serie A last season

Vardy, his wife Rebekah, and their four children struggled during their year in Italy

‘Moving is one of those major changes in life, but moving abroad? Honestly, nobody had prepared me for that. I do think that home is where you make it though. For me it's not bricks and mortar, it's simply where my favourite people are.’

The entire family are now understood to be back in their Grantham home in Lincolnshire, which housed them for much of Vardy’s legendary 13-year stint at Leicester City, where he scored 200 goals in 500 appearances - with 24 of those leading the club to a historic and miraculous Premier League title in 2016.

Once Vardy had returned to the UK, his next step was to decide which club he wanted to move to. There was interest from MLS clubs in the United States, a potential move back to Serie A and even São Paulo in Brazil were interested.

But sources made it clear to Daily Mail Sport that an English club was always Vardy’s preference.

He had a whole host of options on the table, including Championship leaders West Ham, who ended up signing Joel Piroe from Leeds, a number of Premier League teams, a potential fairy tale move to boyhood club Sheffield Wednesday – that was blocked by the EFL – and Hollywood-owned Wrexham attempted to lure him to Wales.

However, Burnley quickly became Vardy’s number one option. They had wanted him after promotion to the Premier League under Scott Parker, and maintained their interest when aware of the striker’s free agency.

The Clarets made it clear to Vardy that he was going to be their main man up top after the departure of Zian Flemming to Ipswich Town, and still hungry to play regularly and compete at the highest level, the former Foxes man was sold on the project.

He has an option of a second year if they get promoted, which may seem unlikely at the time of writing, but is still more than possible if under pressure boss Nicky Hayen can get a tune out of Vardy.

Jamie and Rebekah wanted to relocate back to England after feeling they rushed their decision to move to Italy in 2025

Vardy has now also ventured into podcasting with the Jamie Vardy's Havin' A Party show

Upon signing for the club, he told the club website: ‘I'm really happy to now be here at Burnley. This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town.’

Vardy may be keen to continue as a professional at the top level well into his 40s, but this summer has shown he is already setting up for life away from the pitch.

The Clarets forward wants a piece of the podcasting pie, after seeing the success of Gary Neville and Gary Lineker as media moguls in the ever-evolving landscape of the industry.

With Neville building The Overlap empire and Lineker his Goalhanger platform, which includes the hugely successful The Rest Is Football, Vardy signed with Banijay Entertainment at the start of the summer and has started the Jamie Vardy’s Havin’ A Party podcast.

It has made a flying start, securing a win over Neville’s Overlap by winning the rights to show Bundesliga games. The rights focus on live games. Vardy has also secured a TV deal with Samsung TV, with the mega electronics company creating a dedicated channel, which is also available on Amazon Prime.

The podcast has already gone viral due to former referee Mike Dean’s bombshell admission that he used to play ‘minigames’ while taking charge of Premier League matches.

And while his quotes received backlash, Vardy may have been privately pleased they were made on his show, as he looks to challenge the likes of Neville and Lineker within the footballing podcast industry.

Sports.title: Former Man United star Fred SAVAGES 'piece of c***' ex-manager Erik ten Hag years on from chaotic Old Trafford stint
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has offered a scorching critique of his old manager Erik ten Hag, seasons on from their work together at Old Trafford.

The Brazilian star - who now features for Atletico Mineiro - crossed paths with the Dutch manager for the 2022-23 season, after Ten Hag arrived in Manchester from Ajax.

Ten Hag had been tempted to the club following the departure of Treble-winning icon Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in the dugout, and was hailed as a great tactician upon his arrival.

This was true, Fred contended this week, but 'with the group, he was a piece of c***', tangling particularly strongly with boldfaced names in the squad such as Cristiano Ronaldo and Casemiro.

'He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano, with Casemiro, with Rashford,' the 33-year-old told Charla podcast. 'He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.'

Fred added that with Ten Hag, 'only his Dutch players played.'

Fred did not hold back in his assessment of Erik ten Hag's tenure at Manchester United

'(He was) a clique-ridden coach,' he continued. 'But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.

'He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano (was already) older. He took Cristiano out (of the starting lineup), and then there was a falling out.'

That falling out sent shockwaves through the sport as Ronaldo made clear his desire to leave the club following the 2022 World Cup.

The Real Madrid and Juventus superstar went on to ink an unfathomably lucrative deal to join Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr, sparking a wave of big-money transfers to the Gulf state.

Fred remained at Man United to see out the season and win the Carabao Cup with Ten Hag before a move to Fenerbahce.

His former manager endured a second season at Man United as the club finally welcomed new co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, and despite uneven fortunes in the Premier League, ended the 2023-24 season as FA Cup winners.

Success at Wembley against noisy neighbours Manchester City was enough to secure Ten Hag's future over the summer, but after a challenging start to the following season, Ratcliffe's Ineos leadership group swung the axe in late October.

His replacement Ruben Amorim failed to inspire Man United out of their increasingly disjointed form during his tenure, which stretched to just over a year, with the club moving to install former captain Michael Carrick as interim manager.

An impressive third-place Premier League finish secured him the role on a permanent basis, but has failed to spill into the 2026-27 season, with the Red Devils mired in 12th place ahead of the international break.

Sports.title: Man United handed boost as £70m summer signing Carlos Baleba plays in behind-closed-doors friendly - with Michael Carrick sweating over injury setbacks during international break
Sports.content:
Manchester United have been handed a significant injury boost with summer signing Carlos Baleba playing in a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.

Baleba, who joined the club for £70million from Brighton in the summer, is yet to play for his new side after carrying an ankle injury into the season.

Fans have been anticipating his debut, and it appears that could come sooner rather than later after the 22-year-old featured against Swiss side Lausanne-Sport in a game held at Carrington.

He had been on the bench against Fulham in United's last game before the international break – a 1-1 draw – but did not come on.

United manager Michael Carrick had previously said Baleba was 'pushing to get back as quickly as possible'.

The news comes as a huge boost for United, who have injury concerns amid the three-week international break.

Carlos Baleba featured for Manchester United in a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday

Bruno Fernandes missed Portugal's game against Norway through injury but recovered to start the 4-2 win over Norway.

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus described Fernandes's issue as a 'complicated' shin problem.

Noussair Mazraoui, meanwhile, hobbled off in Morocco's Africa Cup of Nations game against Lesotho earlier this week.

As the Moroccan dived in for a tackle in the 68th minute of the game, he landed awkwardly and immediately signalled towards the bench, appearing in a lot of discomfort.

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo pulled out of England duty before the break, while Amad Diallo, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu are also fitness concerns for United.

The Red Devils' first game back after the break is on October 10, when they will take on Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: OJ Simpson had help killing Nicole Brown and Ronald Goldman, says legendary FBI profiler
Sports.content:
Not only did OJ Simpson commit the 1994 double murder he was famously acquitted of, but the football legend had help with the crime, according to a 22-year veteran of the FBI.

A former New York State prosecutor and FBI profiler who went on to write and produce CBS' Criminal Minds, Jim Clemente supported the theory in a recent podcast interview with media personality Tom Zenner and Kato Kaelin, Simpson's former tenant and a crucial witness in his murder trial.

Simpson was infamously acquitted for the murders of his ex-wife Nicole Brown and her friend Ronald Goldman in October of 1995 only to be found financially liable for their wrongful deaths at a civil trial 16 months later. Both trials included graphic photographs of a horrifying crime scene, where Goldman and Brown were brutally stabbed to death on June 12, 1994.

Simpson's ties to that crime scene on LA's Bundy Drive are notorious. There was his blood and DNA, not to mention bloody shoe prints matching his size-12 Bruno Maglis. There was even a bloody trail leading from the crime scene to his white Ford Bronco and onto his own property.

But according to Clemente, evidence points to another attacker at the scene. For starters, he explained that the presence of multiple stabbing victims always increases the likelihood of multiple attackers, simply because it's difficult for one person to commit both crimes quickly and in the same space.

The bigger clues, Clemente explained, were the defensive wounds left on Goldman's legs.

OJ Simpson denied murdering his ex-wife Nicole Brown (left) and her friend Ronald Goldman

The body of Nicole Brown Simpson is seen where she was found on the bloodstained walkway of her Bundy Drive condominium as seen in this LAPD evidence photo from June of 1994

Goldman wasn't believed to be an intended target, but was nonetheless murdered with Brown

'With the cuts in his jeans, in his pants that he was wearing at the time, the knife wounds could only have been made if both of his legs were elevated and bent and straightened out like he was kicking,' Clemente sad.

'And the only way that we behaviorally could figure out how that could happen is if somebody has him in a bear hug from behind and he's being stabbed by somebody in the front.

'He's kicking, he's fighting for his life,' Clemente continued. 'It's a horrible, horrible scene.'

Curiously, Clemente explained, Goldman did not have defensive wounds on his arms.

'If he was punching and kicking, you would see the same kinds of wounds through his clothing on his arms because the person with the knife would have been lashing out,' Clemente said. 'He wouldn't just stab his legs.'

Rather, according to Clemente, Goldman's 'arms are being held and his arms were being pinned and that's why he resorted to his legs only.'

As for why Simpson would bring an accomplice to murder his wife, Clemente suggested the presence of the couple's two children at her condominium was a good reason.

'What if the kids aren't in bed yet?' Clemente asked, rhetorically. 'What if the kids wake up and come down?'

Kato Kaelin (left) sits alongside former FBI profiler Jim Clemente on Tom Zenner's podcast

Clemente (right) told Zenner (left) that Goldman's defensive wounds point to an accomplice

OJ is pictured during the 1995 double-murder trial. He was ultimately acquitted by the jury

Simpson continued to deny any involvement in the Brown-Goldman murders until his death from cancer at age 76 in 2024, but the theory he committed the crimes with an accomplice is nothing new.

Recently, The Daily Mail revealed an upcoming Peacock documentary investigating the theory that Simpson had a mob-linked accomplice in the late Joey Ippolito Jr. What's more, The Daily Mail reviewed unauthorized clips of the documentary showing Ippolito's brothers discussing their deceased sibling's potential involvement in the crime.

Peacock spokespeople declined to comment on The Daily Mail's reporting at the time. The project's upcoming release has since been confirmed by other outlets.

Speaking with Zenner, Clemente also challenged the notion that the murders were simply a crime of passion.

Rather, he insisted Brown was the intended victim of a carefully planned murder.

Goldman, sadly, was just returning the pair of glasses Brown left at his restaurant when he stumbled upon the crime that was taking place.

'Whoever committed this crime had an extreme amount of rage and anger in them,' Clemente told Zenner and Kaelin. 'And they have been fantasizing about this for a long time. They planned this. This is this is not a disorganized crime. This is an organized crime. Which means that the offender thought about this, thought it out carefully, thought about every angle, knew when she would be vulnerable.

'Of course, he thought she would be alone at that moment, but because she left the glasses there at the restaurant, somebody else showed up. That is an unexpected result.'

Asked if he had any clue about the accomplice's identity, Clemente said he had a 'pretty good idea' who was with Simpson but stopped short of revealing a name.

Of course, there is no statute of limitations on murder, so if such an accomplice us still alive, they could theoretically face justice.

Bombshell OJ Simpson claim unmasks accomplice that could blow the case wide open: New documentary reveals fresh allegations that NFL legend had help in double murder

Sports.title: Man City whistleblower launches £2.55m fundraiser after losing his witness protection just days after Premier League found the club guilty of serious financial breaches
Sports.content:
The Man City whistleblower whose hacked emails played a role in sparking the Premier League's investigation into the club's finances has lost his witness protection in Portugal, and is looking to raise over £2.55million to 'relocate within the next few days'. Through his Football Leaks site, Pinto released thousands of confidential documents, including confidential emails from inside Man City, which formed the basis for reporting by Der Spiegel in 2018. This in turn launched probes from both UEFA and the Premier League into the club's practices, the latter's investigation coming to a head this week with the confirmation of a guilty verdict on all of their serious breaches of the league's financial regulations. Due to his high profile, the hacker had been under witness protection in his native Portugal since 2020, after agreeing to cooperate with the authorities by providing information from his Football Leaks files. In a statement shared by his lawyers, Pinto appealed to the Portuguese authorities for a decision laden with 'serious consequences' that was akin to 'state terrorism'. 'Rui Pinto, the whistleblower who was at the origin of Football Leaks, was notified last Wednesday that the special security program from which he has benefited since August 2020 will end on October 10,' the statement read. 'In just a few days, without having been heard beforehand, as the law requires, he will lose the protected and confidential residence that was assigned to him and will be forced to urgently find new housing, with no guarantee that police protection will be maintained. Portuguese hacker and Football League founder Rui Pinto has seen his witness protection removed (pictured in 2023) 'His situation is now critical. The threats against him are not merely theoretical: last April, he was assaulted in Lisbon. His revelations involved powerful figures with vast resources, and many of the resulting judicial proceedings are still ongoing, as evidenced by the decision issued just a few days ago by the Premier League's independent commission regarding Manchester City. 'Abruptly deprived of his protected residence and placed in a situation of extreme precariousness, Rui Pinto will now be more vulnerable than at any other moment since 2020.' Pinto was handed a four-year suspended sentence in 2020 after he was found guilty by the Portuguese courts of illegal access to data and attempted extortion. Such was his concern over his safety that he sported a bulletproof vest to attend his trial, which also saw a ramping-up of security measures around the courtroom. The 37-year-old's lawyers stressed that his cooperation with 'Portuguese justice' justified the continuation of his protection programme, and urged the Ministry of Justice to reconsider its position. But with no u-turn in sight, Pinto took drastic action, launching a GoFundMe crowdfunding campaign with a target of £2.55m (€3m) to allow him to urgently move to an 'undisclosed location'. Pinto cited 'multiple death threats and the serious risk of an assassination attempt' as reason for why such a flight from his home country might be necessary. 'I am asking for everyone's support to help me survive this serious situation created by the Portuguese State, which, as I have already stated, has knowingly decided to place my life at risk,' his personal statement added. In the early stages of the fundraiser, Pinto has managed to raise just over £14,000 (€16,582).

Your browser does not support iframes.

Earlier in 2026, Pinto was involved in another lengthy trial, which saw him acquitted of over 241 counts of illegally accessing email accounts belonging to a number of sporting organisations. Man City continue to deny that they deployed 'sham' contracts and disguised over £900m in sponsorship payments in the wake of the Premier League sharing the core decision made by the independent commission on Tuesday. They have since launched their appeal, with the club adamant that they hold 'irrefutable evidence' of their innocence. Daily Mail Sport revealed that much of their defence will suggest that commercial contracts were paid for by the Abu Dhabi government rather than their owner. But this could, in turn, counteract an argument made by Abu Dhabi airline - and key Man City sponsor - Etihad to the United States' department of commerce, transportation and state in 2015. As part of an investigation into state-owned airlines, Etihad shared the following statement: 'We are government-owned and have been since our founding. 'We are and have always been clear that we do not receive any subsidies from the Abu Dhabi government, and that we are financed through a combination of equity, shareholder and commercial loans. 'Our shareholder's equity and loans are not subsidies under any applicable definition; they are the means by which the Abu Dhabi government has sensibly invested in a successful business model.' New Premier League rules state that a hearing must be held within 12 weeks of an appeal being lodged, with a decision due within 30 days of the hearing, which can only last five days, concluding. Any punishment could, therefore, be imposed this season.

Sports.title: Max Verstappen qualifies on pole for the first time in TEN MONTHS at uprooted Bahrain Grand Prix - as George Russell finishes eighth in blow to his title hopes against Kimi Antonelli
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen qualifies on pole for the first time in TEN MONTHS at uprooted Bahrain Grand Prix - as George Russell finishes eighth in blow to his title hopes against Kimi Antonelli

Just when you see a door opening, it shuts.

It may yet be that George Russell can unlock his world championship hopes in the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' which has been relocated to Malaysia owing to the war in the Middle East.

But qualifying, where the indefatigable Max Verstappen took his first pole position of the season represented a serious problem for the British driver.

For while Kimi Antonelli set the fourth-fastest time, promoted to third on the grid after Isack Hadjar took an engine penalty, Russell was a distant eighth in the other Mercedes, albeit moved up a place for the same reason. It was Russell's worst qualifying performance of the year.

The one-slot elevation apart, this was a big blow for our one national hope of title success, who lies 66 points behind championship-leader Antonelli with eight rounds remaining. Yes, Russell won in Azerbaijan a week ago, a result that could have acted as a spark to reignite the ambition of his lifetime. But this was back to earth with a bump.

His qualifying session was an elbow in the ribs, not least given that Mercedes introduced an upgrade here. Russell was 0.240 of a second back from Antonelli.

Max Verstappen will start the uprooted Bahrain Grand Prix on pole after Saturday's qualifying

George Russell will start Sunday's race in eighth, in a damaging blow to his title hopes

Yet, speaking afterwards in the humid Sepang paddock, Russell remained upbeat, as he needed to be going into today's gruelling race. 'There is going to be a lot happening tomorrow,' he said. 'The tyre degradation is huge and race pace will be king so even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.'

Asked why it had been a poor weekend up to that point, he said: 'I don't know. This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the Tarmac.

'The lap times nine years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.

'All our internal numbers say the upgrade is an improvement, but obviously we need to follow the lap times and not what the numbers suggest. The numbers look absolutely fine, and in line with expectations. However, the result wasn't.'

Lewis Hamilton qualified second for Ferrari, three-tenths off the top with Verstappen's team-mate Hadjar third at that point, prior to his sanction.

'I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow,' said Hamilton. 'If we are in the fight that would be awesome. I've been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.'

Charles Leclerc was fifth best, though he was later promoted on Hadjar's relegation, and Lando Norris sixth, a place ahead of his McLaren pal Oscar Piastri.

Related to the subject of Norris, Franco Colapinto qualified 15th but will take at least a five-place grid penalty. That is a result of the accident he caused in Azerbaijan a week ago that put both his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and the world champion (Norris) out of the race.

The Argentine may suffer a further sanction if, as it seems likely, he takes on a new engine. So he will go to the back of the grid.

In unexpected news, the two Aston Martins made it out of Q1, a rare occurrence. Their recent upgrades seemed to have had some rejuvenating effect, as Fernando Alonso qualified 12th and Lance Stroll 14th.

The bottom spots went to the Cadillac pair of Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

On the subject of Norris, Franco Colapinto qualified 15th but will take at least a five-place grid penalty. That is a result of the accident he caused in Azerbaijan a week ago that put both his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and world champion Norris out of the race.

The Brazilian may suffer a further sanction if, as seems likely, he takes on a new engine.

In unexpected news, the two Aston Martins made it out of Q1, a rare occurrence. Their upgrades seemed to have had some rejuvenating effect, as Fernando Alonso qualified 12th and Lance Stroll 14th.

The bottom spots went to the Cadillac pair of Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha reveals what Mohamed Salah told him before leaving Liverpool
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha reveals what Mohamed Salah told him before leaving Liverpool

Liverpool star Rio Ngumoha could make his third appearance for England against Croatia on Saturday evening and will hope to harness some valuable advice from former teammate Mohamed Salah

View 2 Images Mo Salah shared some words of wisdom with Rio Ngumoha

Rio Ngumoha has praised Mohamed Salah for help at Liverpool ahead of a potential full England debut. The Reds wonderkid was a surprise inclusion in Thomas Tuchel's England squad ahead of the World Cup.

‌



‌



He retained his place in the selection for the first international break of the campaign and was afforded a brief cameo against Czechia in Prague. Ngumoha could yet earn his first start in upcoming games against Croatia and the second game against Czechia.

‌



And he will hope to harness advice from Liverpool hero Salah, who told the youngster to prioritise his end product before departing Anfield. Speaking to The FA, he said: "The player who I probably learned the most from is Mohamed Salah, when he was at Liverpool.

‌



"He taught me a lot, especially towards the back end when he knew he was leaving. He helped me a lot.

"Like he always says about looking at his numbers and he was always telling me: 'Rio, you know you're a good player but to reach the top, you have to add the goals and assists'.

"And it will come naturally but he was just going through little things like that [with me]. When he first started [talking to me], it was like: 'Wow! I've been watching you since I was young and you're telling me how to [improve]. Like, you're helping me and you're guiding me.'

"But then over time, I saw him as a very good team-mate and he was helping me a lot, so I can thank him much more."

‌



On his fledgling England career, Ngumoha added: "I definitely had the confidence to believe I could wear the England shirt at 18.

View 2 Images Rio Ngumoha received advice from Mo Salah at Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

"Did I think it'd be the first camp? Maybe not. But I definitely knew that I'd be playing one day when I was still pretty young.

‌



"I was ready to go [when coming on], Once I knew I was coming on, I just had the hunger, the fight, the belief.

"And once I was on the pitch, it was like any game of football really. I think, you know, Jude is 23 and is already probably the best midfielder in the world at this point.

"And he definitely believed that he would play in an England shirt at 17, same as Wayne Rooney, what he did for his club, his country, hopefully I can do the same. It's going to be a good journey I think, yes."

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or winner's son joins non-league side after Chelsea and Tottenham exits
Sports.content:
Ballon d'Or winner's son joins non-league side after Chelsea and Tottenham exits

The Ballon d'Or winner's son will be hoping he can cut his cloth in English football after leaving Chelsea and Tottenham

View 2 Images Kristian Shevchenko has joined Sholing in English football's seventh tier (Image: (Photo by Javier TORRES / AFP via Getty Images))

The son of Ballon d'Or winner Andriy Shevchenko has joined a non-league side after spending time with Premier League clubs Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur. 19-year-old Kristian Shevchenko spent time with the London sides in 2022 and 2023, before joining Watford afterwards.

‌



‌



The forward, who has 15 caps for Ukraine at youth level, left the Hornets earlier this summer, but has finally found a new club in non-league side Sholing. The winger has linked up with the seventh-tier Southern League side ahead of Saturday’s FA Cup third-round qualifier at Ebbsfleet.

‌



Sholing have taken ten points from their opening eight league games and find themselves in 16th place.

‌



Arsene Wenger was right to be fuming about Man City - now football owes him an apology READ MORE :

Man Utd and players could be due millions as 'review' held after Man City charges READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In a statement released on social media, Sholing said: "Join us in welcoming our new signing, Kristian Shevchenko!

"The 19-year-old joins the Boatmen having developed through the youth setups at Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Watford, signing his first professional contract with the Hornets in 2025.

‌



"Kristian also represented Ukraine at the 2025 U20 World Cup, bringing international youth experience to SO19. Welcome to the Boatmen."

View 2 Images Andriy Shevchenko was a legendary forward during his playing days (Image: (Photo by Danylo Antoniuk/Anadolu via Getty Images))

Kristian's father, Andriy, won the Ballon d'Or in 2004 and had a glittering career across European football. He's a cult hero at AC Milan and played for Chelsea and Dynamo Kyiv.

‌



During his time in Italy, Shevchenko won the Serie A, Coppa Italia and Champions League titles in an eight-year stint at the San Siro, split across two spells.

He moved to Stamford Bridge in 2006 but couldn't quite reach the lofty heights he'd shown in Italy, though he still managed to win the League Cup and FA Cup.

Kristian's career may not have gotten off to the start to suggest he'll go on to mimic his famous father, but he'll be hoping the move to Sholing can kick-start his career in English football.

Article continues below

The youngster has been a regular for Ukraine's U20s side, but didn't manage a single first-team appearance for Watford after signing a professional contract with the club in 2025.

He was released by the Championship outfit during the summer and has finally found a new home in Hampshire.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: UAE threaten Andy Burnham, Rui Pinto goes into hiding, appeal statement
Sports.content:
Manchester City continue to fight the charges levelled at them by the Premier League

The latest news and opinion on the Manchester City charges after the club officially appealed the guilty verdict on all but one of the 115 charges levelled at them

Good morning and welcome to our live blog on Manchester City's extraordinary 115 charges case. City were found guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

The independent commission found that City had arranged 'sham contracts' and relied on 'sham agreements' to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £900million and reduce its costs.

The club released a short statement on Friday , revealing it had appealed the independent commission's guilty verdict and maintained their innocence, despite strong statements from the Premier League and FA. They claimed the ruling included 'clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.'

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also waded into the mess, with reports claiming a punishment for Manchester City could impact the UAE's interest in future major investments in the United Kingdom. That follows on from the former Mayor of Manchester saying he would be "really concerned" to lose City's investors, after working closely with them on development projects in Manchester.

You can follow all the latest news, updates and opinions in our live blog below.

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger was right to be fuming about Man City - now football owes him an apology
Sports.content:
Back in the summer of 2011, Arsene Wenger had reached the end of his tether.

Wenger was as frustrated as many people had ever seen him as he spoke to three of us in a little corridor outside a dressing room after a draw with Hangzhou Greentown in Yiwu on a pre-season tour of China and Malaysia.

Manchester City, who had signed Emmanuel Adebayor and Kolo Toure two years earlier, were courting yet more Arsenal players and Roberto Mancini had openly spoken about wanting to sign Samir Nasri.

It was on that tour that Wenger had also questioned City’s £400m sponsorship deal with Etihad Airways as he described it as “Platini’s big test.” Michel Platini was championing UEFA Financial Fair Play.

‌



UEFA’s rules were just coming in and Wenger was incredulous when talking about out City’s world record 10-year deal.

Don't miss John Cross' exclusive newsletter every Friday - just for Mirror+ subscribers - CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP

The deal was struck with Etihad which, a few of us wrote at the time, was “owned by the Abu Dhabi government and has close links to the City owner, Sheikh Mansour, a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family.” We didn’t know our words would come back like this.

It dwarfed Arsenal’s deal with another airline, Emirates, which was £90m over 15 years. They were incredibly similar as they were big commercial deals and stadium naming rights.

"We must have done a bad deal,” said Wenger with a huge dash of sarcasm. City described Wenger’s comments as "unfounded and regrettable” and insisted the figures were “not accurate.”

‌



And it was against that background that Wenger felt utterly powerless. City’s sponsorship deal dwarfed Arsenal’s. And now City were cherry picking all of Arsenal’s best players.

Wenger, talking about Mancini’s public pursuit of Nasri, said: “These comments are not allowed. They are against the basic rules of football.

View 3 Images Wenger was fuming when Roberto Mancini managed to sign Samir Nasri from Arsenal

“We want is respect and we don't make these comments about players who are under contract at other clubs. It's time football in England came back to these basic rules.”

‌



He was so angry as he spoke in that little corridor. I remember it so clearly. There was only two or three of us there. He could barely contain his rage.

Wenger was fighting with one hand behind his back. But, let’s be clear, he was in there still fighting. It was a miracle that Wenger even kept Arsenal competitive. Look at the difference in figures.

Wenger used to call it “financial doping.” It was his pet subject. And, looking back, Wenger called it first. His insight, knowledge and campaigning was unparalleled.

The back pages carried his words day after day, week after week. Don’t listen to anyone who says no-one listened.

‌



But, unfortunately, football did not listen closely enough. Yes, the Premier League brought in its own financial rules and restrictions. But it feels like football failed him even though he was clearly years ahead of everyone else.

That is why football owes Arsene Wenger an apology.

'A miracle other teams could compete'

That summer of 2011, Wenger started by insisting Arsenal would not sell both Nasri and Cesc Fabregas in the same window.

‌



Nasri had his heart set on City. His teammates would rib him that he should stop driving round the M25 and head straight for Manchester. The deal was done.

Fabregas had his heart set on Barcelona. That is maybe more understandable because he was a boyhood fan and was always going to return one day.

They both went eventually and Wenger was made to look weak which was grossly unfair. Ultimately, Wenger was utterly powerless to stop two of his best players departing in the same summer.

Why?

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal lost Samir Nasri, Emmanuel Adebayor and Gael Clichy...all to Man City

Because when City came in at that time they always got their man. Toure, Adebayor, Nasri, Gael Clichy and Bacary Sagna all went on the same path.

All of this really should put in perspective the scale of City’s alleged breaches. Sometimes we get lost in the legalities of it all. The sheer scale and the financial complexities of it all. Who owns what and so on. It’s draining.

But putting it in pure and simple football terms offers far more context. City’s commercial deals - which were described by the Premier League commission as “artificially inflated” - allowed them to spend bigger and sign all of their rivals’ best players.

‌



The Arsenal and Wenger case study is so clear. It is, quite frankly, a miracle that other teams were able to compete and beat City during those times.

Sports.title: Ireland boss warns second Israel clash will ‘not be a friendly’ after ‘hate’ comment
Sports.content:
Ireland boss warns Israel clash will ‘not be a friendly’ as press conference descends into chaos

The Republic of Ireland are set to take on Israel for the second time during the international break with tensions having seemingly boiled over ahead of their rematch in Serbia

View 2 Images Heimir Hallgrimsson has spoken ahead of his side's second clash with Israel (Image: Getty Images)

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrímsson has vowed that the nation’s second game against Israel ‘is not going to be a friendly’ with the press conference ahead of the game cancelled. The two sides were scheduled to come together twice over the international break, with tempers simmering between the two countries.

‌



‌



Last week’s clash was in major doubt, with calls for Ireland to boycott the match due to Israel's military action in Gaza. A UN-commissioned inquiry previously found Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians in war-torn Gaza.

‌



More than 73,000 people have been killed after Israeli military action was launched in response to the Hamas attack on the Nova Festival in southern Israel of October 7 2023, which killed approximately 1,200 people.

‌



However, despite goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu deciding to not participate, after a team vote, his Ireland team-mates ultimately decide to fulfil the fixture.

Ireland won that game 3-0 with goals from Troy Parrot, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan. Ahead of their second showdown, hostilities appear to have grown.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Israel and West Ham winger Manor Solomon said: “Obviously they hate us, and we don’t like them.”

In response, Ireland boss Hallgrimsson said: “This is not going to be a friendly. That’s why I’m saying that we need to use every second between now and the game to recover, to collect energy and be ready for the game not only physically but mentally.

‌



“It will be tricky and challenging for the players to be ready. The medical team will work day and night to get them fit and fresh for that game. It’s just another football match but there’s more at stake for all of us.”

Away from Hallgrimmsson's comments, the pre-match press conference ahead of the game descended into chaos with an Israeli journalist seemingly accusing the Irish players of racism during their last meeting, an accusation that was strongly denied by Kieran Crowley. He abruptly ended the press conference and was only willing to speak to Irish media in the dressing room.

Ireland are set to fly to Serbia for the game, with it being considered their ‘home’ game. And he has claimed that the sense of feeling from supporters has been made loud and clear.

‌



He said: “I’m not going to lie. I didn’t know what to expect. The Stop The Game protest is loud. I don’t know how many but it has been loud.

“It was just good to see the support from the fans. I just want to repeat the appreciation for the fans showing up and supporting the players.

View 2 Images Manor Solomon fired a brutal comment at Ireland after their initial meeting (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“It helped us a lot, giving us more pride to play for the country. We all feel more appreciated now than before this match.”

This weekend’s game is set to take place in Backa Topola in Northern Serbia. Asked what he knows about the town, Hallgrimsson replied: “Absolutely nothing.

“I just know that we’re staying in the hotel at the stadium. Also that it’s a one-and-a-half hour drive from the airport and a really good hotel they said. I didn’t need to know anything else.”

Article continues below

He added: “This four game window has been challenging and testing. It will be different, going from playing in front of 45,000 supporters to an empty stadium. This is another angle to this story and we just need to be ready for this one.”

Following their clash against Israel, Ireland will round off their fixtures with a showdown with Austria in Linz. As it stands, Hallgrimsson’s side sit third in their group with four points from three games.

Sports.title: Southampton see appeal dismissed in major boost for EFL side as Spygate verdict looms
Sports.content:
Southampton see appeal dismissed in major boost for EFL side as Spygate verdict looms

Southampton are nervously waiting the result of the FA’s investigation into their Spygate scandal that saw them kicked out of the play-offs, but the Championship side have already secured another win in the courtroom

View 2 Images Tonda Eckert is still awaiting the FA verdict into the Spygate scandal (Image: Getty Images)

Southampton have secured a major win after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in their favour following a transfer dispute with Brazilian side Atletico Mineiro. The argument revolves around defender Lyanco, who left the Saints back in 2024.

‌



‌



Southampton agreed to sell the defender for around €5.2million (£4.5m) in the aftermath of their promotion back to the Premier League via the play-offs. That fee was intended to be payable over five instalments running until July 2026.

‌



According to Globo Esporte, Southampton went to FIFA claiming that the third payment had not been received, with their Dispute Resolution Chamber siding with the English side. Atletico Mineiro then appealed that decision with the CAS, but they too have ruled in the Saints’ favour and they will now receive €1.125m (£980k) plus interest for the delayed payment. The Brazilian side reportedly has 45 days to pay up.

‌



That could even be added to, with it being suggested that Southampton notified their Brazilian colleagues that they had also missed the deadline for January’s payment, with FIFA again being dragged into the dispute.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



And once again, they ruled in Southampton’s favour, with FIFA rejecting Atletico’s argument that they had not received updated and valid invoices. Should the Brazilian side fail to pay, they could potentially be hit with multi-window registration bans.

But the decision will be a welcome boost to Southampton, who are awaiting the verdict of the FA’s probe into the Spygate scandal that saw them booted out of the playoffs last season. Speaking to BBC Sport last month, boss Tonda Eckert said: "I had a long meeting with the FA. There's one side to the story from the press, so I had my chance to sit down.

"I talked the FA through everything that happened. Now it's up to them to make a decision. I don't really have any emotions towards that.

‌



View 2 Images Lyanco left Southampton for Atletico Mineiro in 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

"We're so long into the process, the FA is going to decide what they decide, and move on. My impression from the hearing was that they listened to me.

"We sat for almost four hours, so it's been quite a long conversation. The club received a big, big punishment. A big punishment.

Article continues below

"I think it's a punishment that is absolutely unheard of in the history of sports. And it's tough for me to say that because obviously it concerns me.

"But I've asked for forgiveness for what I've done. I've apologised publicly. I think the punishment has been very hard on the club. The rest is not for me to decide."

Sports.title: Jack Wilshere offers honest Max Dowman verdict with Arsenal open to loan exit
Sports.content:
Jack Wilshere offers honest Max Dowman verdict with Arsenal open to loan exit

Max Dowman is one of the most promising young players to come out of Arsenal’s academy over recent years, with former midfielder Jack Wilshere a huge fan of his talent

View 2 Images Max Dowman continues to shine at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Jack Wilshere has sung the praises of Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman - with even his dad claiming he is better than the former Gunners star. Dowman, 16, enjoyed a standout breakout season last term as he made 13 first-team appearances and scored once.

‌



‌



The youngster collected a host of records along the way as he became the youngest Premier League winner, Arsenal’s youngest ever starter, the youngest ever Champions League player and the youngest player to have started in the Premier League.

‌



Fellow academy graduate Wilshere has claimed that Dowman’s talent was evident early on, with his own dad even claiming that the youngster was better than the former midfielder.

‌



"Max played for my 18s team when he was 13," Wilshere said in an interview with BBC Sport. "I remember calling my dad because I played for the 18s when I was 14. I was like, 'was 13 too young?'

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"In the first game we could clearly see that he was ready for it. And I remember calling my dad and saying, 'you need to come watch this kid'. My dad did, and my dad's very biased, as you could imagine. But even he said, 'he's better than you'."

Dowman has continued his development this season, having shone and scored twice in a Carabao Cup win against Ipswich Town and it has been suggested that the North London side are open to a loan move. Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has been key to Dowman’s progression, while Wilshere has hailed him as a huge influence on his own fledgling managerial career.

"I got to see Mikel and how he coached and the influence he was having," he added. "I would ask him questions, why he's doing certain things, and I started to fall in love with it and how he started to prepare training sessions.

‌



View 2 Images Jack Wilshere has successfully moved into management (Image: Getty Images)

"I'd get an opportunity to practice that with the 18s in the afternoon and it was something I wasn't that good at, and I felt uncomfortable at times.

"I was influenced by Mikel, but then I had to learn how to teach. I had to learn how to get that across, how to plan a session and how to get the outcomes that you wanted.

Article continues below

"I played under some good coaches and was quite good at understanding what a coach wants, but I never dived into 'why is he asking me to do that?' Mikel really made that clear and I was lucky enough to have a relationship where I could say, 'well, why do you want that?' And he was open enough to share it with me."

Sports.title: The 50 hardest Manchester United players to ever walk out at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Manchester United have welcomed a healthy portion of the Premier League's hardest stars through their doors over the years. However, the club's reputation as a landing zone for some of England's most notorious tough nuts dates back way further.

From the Busby Babes era to Ron Atkinson's reign, Sir Alex Ferguson's iconic teams and beyond, the club is renowned for housing hard characters. And Michael Carrick's squad of today could perhaps do with reviving that tradition in its bid to get back on top of the European order.

Not every intimidating character has been so fortunate to combine those traits with the same degree of quality on the pitch. That being said, Mirror Football has compiled a list of the hardest players to have pulled on the iconic red over the decades.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
