World.title: Opeth Plays Espaço Unimed in São Paulo on 6 November
World.content:
BRAZIL · MUSIC

Key Facts — What Swedish progressive metal band Opeth plays its Latin American run in São Paulo.

— When Friday 6 November 2026. Doors 19:00, show 21:30.

— Where Espaço Unimed, Rua Tagipuru 795, Barra Funda, São Paulo.

— Tickets Eventim Brasil and the venue box office, from R$350 (about US$67) for Pista to R$700 (about US$134) for Camarote A, at the RT rate of 2 October 2026 (about R$5.22 per US$). Half price is 50%.

— Good to know Barra Funda terminal has Metro Line 3 and CPTM trains. Age rules apply.

A Friday night for progressive metal in São Paulo, with Brazil’s other Opeth date in Curitiba the night before.

Opeth play Espaço Unimed in São Paulo, Brazil, on Friday 6 November 2026. Doors open at 19:00 and the show starts at 21:30. Eventim Brasil lists tickets from R$350 (about US$67) for Pista to R$700 (about US$134) for Camarote A.

Who Opeth are

Opeth formed in Stockholm in 1990 and became one of the best-known progressive metal bands in the world. Their songs mix heavy riffs with long, quiet passages and complex arrangements.

Their 2024 album is called The Last Will and Testament. If you are new to the band, expect long songs and a calm, attentive crowd. No support act is confirmed for the São Paulo date.

The Latin American run starts in Santiago on 1 November and continues in Buenos Aires on 3 November. Brazil has two dates, Curitiba on 5 November at the Ópera de Arame and São Paulo on 6 November. The run then moves to Bogotá on 8 November and Mexico City on 11 November.

A concert crowd at Espaço Unimed (formerly Espaço das Américas), São Paulo. File photo.

Tickets step by step

Eventim Brasil is the official online seller, and the Unimed box office also sells tickets without a fee. Pista costs R$350 (about US$67), Premium costs R$560 (about US$107), Mezanino costs R$600 (about US$115), Camarote B costs R$650 (about US$124) and Camarote A costs R$700 (about US$134).

Half-price tickets cost 50% of these prices for eligible groups, with proof. It is not clear from the sources whether online fees are included, so check the total at checkout. Eventim offers instalments of four payments without interest and up to ten with interest.

The dollar values use the RT market rate of 2 October 2026, about R$5.22 per US$.

Venue, age rules and getting there

Espaço Unimed is at Rua Tagipuru 795 in Barra Funda, in the west of São Paulo. It was formerly called Espaço das Américas. Doors open at 19:00 and the show starts at 21:30.

Barra Funda terminal, with Metro Line 3 (Red), CPTM trains and long-distance buses, is the nearest transport hub. Ride-hailing apps are the alternative after the show.

The age rule is 16 for entry without an adult. Younger people must come with a parent or guardian. Bring a photo ID.

What else to do in São Paulo that week

The Memorial da América Latina, in Barra Funda, is a short ride from the venue. Vila Madalena has bars and street art, and the Avenida Paulista has the main museums.

November is early summer, with warm days and heavy afternoon showers. Leave extra time for traffic, because Friday evenings are busy in the west of the city.

When do Opeth play in São Paulo?

Opeth play Espaço Unimed on Friday 6 November 2026. Doors open at 19:00 and the show starts at 21:30.

How much are Opeth tickets in São Paulo?

Eventim Brasil lists R$350 (about US$67) to R$700 (about US$134), at about R$5.22 per US$. Half price is 50%. Check the final total at checkout.

What is the age limit for the Opeth concert?

Entry without an adult is from age 16. Younger people must come with a parent or guardian.

How do I get to Espaço Unimed?

The venue is at Rua Tagipuru 795 in Barra Funda. The Barra Funda terminal has Metro Line 3 (Red), CPTM trains and buses.

World.title: Maro Plays Circo Voador in Rio de Janeiro on 3 November
World.content:
BRAZIL · MUSIC

Key Facts — What Portuguese singer-songwriter Maro plays the So Much Has Changed tour in Rio.

— When Tuesday 3 November 2026. Doors 20:00, start time listed as 20:00 on Eventim.

— Where Circo Voador, Rua dos Arcos s/n, Lapa, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

— Tickets Eventim Brasil, half price R$100 (about US$19) to R$150 (about US$29) and full price R$200 (about US$38) to R$300 (about US$57), in three batches, at the RT rate of 2 October 2026 (about R$5.22 per US$).

— Good to know Age 18 and over; from 14 with a parent. Fees at checkout are not confirmed.

A Portuguese singer-songwriter plays Circo Voador in Lapa on a Tuesday night, with three price batches on sale.

Maro plays Circo Voador in Lapa, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on Tuesday 3 November 2026. Eventim Brasil lists half-price tickets from R$100 (about US$19) and full-price tickets up to R$300 (about US$57). The show is for ages 18 and over, or from 14 with a parent.

Who Maro is

Maro is the stage name of the Portuguese singer-songwriter Mariana Secca. She co-wrote “saudade, saudade”, the song that represented Portugal at the Eurovision Song Contest in 2022.

If you do not know her work, start with “saudade, saudade”. The tour is called So Much Has Changed. In Brazil it also plays Belo Horizonte on 4 November and São Paulo on 7 November.

The Lapa arches in Rio de Janeiro, near the venue. File photo. Photo: Solange Maria, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Tickets step by step

Eventim Brasil is the ticket seller. Tickets were released in three batches, called lotes. Lote 1 costs R$100 (about US$19) half price or R$200 (about US$38) full price. Lote 2 costs R$120 (about US$23) or R$240 (about US$46). Lote 3 costs R$150 (about US$29) or R$300 (about US$57).

Half price, called meia-entrada, applies to students, seniors and some other groups, with proof. Check the Eventim page for the rules. The dollar values use the RT market rate of 2 October 2026, about R$5.22 per US$. The service fee at checkout is not confirmed.

Avoid buying from social media accounts. Use the official Eventim page.

Venue, age rules and getting there

Circo Voador is at Rua dos Arcos, in the Lapa district. Eventim lists doors and the start at 20:00. Check the page before the date, since a start time at the same hour as doors can change.

Arrive early. Doors and the start are listed at the same hour, and no support act has been announced. Keep your ticket on your phone and bring photo ID for the age check.

The age rating is 18 and over. Young people from 14 can enter with a parent or guardian, according to the ticket page.

Lapa is busy at night, and ride-hailing apps are the simple way home. Keep your phone and valuables close in the crowded streets around the arches.

What else to do in Rio that week

The Lapa arches and the Escadaria Selarón steps are a short walk from the venue. Santa Teresa, the hilltop district above Lapa, has cafés and views.

November is early summer in Rio, with heat and sudden storms, so carry a light rain jacket. A Tuesday show leaves time for Sugarloaf or the beaches during the day.

When does Maro play in Rio de Janeiro?

Maro plays Circo Voador on Tuesday 3 November 2026. Eventim lists doors and the start at 20:00.

How much are Maro tickets in Rio?

Eventim lists half price from R$100 (about US$19) and full price up to R$300 (about US$57), at about R$5.22 per US$. Fees at checkout are not confirmed.

Circo Voador is at Rua dos Arcos, in the Lapa district of Rio de Janeiro, close to the Lapa arches.

World.title: National Crafts Fair Opens in Belo Horizonte on 2 Dec
World.content:
BRAZIL · CRAFTS

Key Facts — What The Feira Nacional de Artesanato, a national crafts fair with more than 3,000 craftspeople.

— When Wednesday 2 to Sunday 6 December 2026. Wednesday to Friday 14:00 to 22:00, Saturday 10:00 to 22:00, Sunday 10:00 to 21:00.

— Where Expominas, Avenida Amazonas 6200, Gameleira, Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais.

— Tickets Sympla, with payment in up to 12 instalments. The 2026 price is not published; 2025 tickets cost R$20 (about US$4).

— Good to know Metro station Gameleira serves the venue. The organiser is Centro Cape.

Five days of Brazilian handicrafts under one roof, in the capital of Minas Gerais.

The Feira Nacional de Artesanato runs from Wednesday 2 to Sunday 6 December 2026 at Expominas in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. Sympla says more than 3,000 craftspeople take part. Tickets are sold on Sympla, but the 2026 price has not been published.

What the fair is

The Feira Nacional de Artesanato is a national crafts fair organised by Centro Cape. It gathers craftspeople from many Brazilian regions in one pavilion in Belo Horizonte.

For a foreigner in Brazil, it is a one-stop way to see regional work such as ceramics, textiles, wood and leather. It is also a good place to buy gifts before the holidays, and to meet the makers.

Sympla lists more than 3,000 craftspeople. Earlier press figures for the number of stands and visitors are not confirmed, so we do not repeat them.

The Edifício JK, designed by Oscar Niemeyer, in Belo Horizonte. File photo.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Tickets and prices

Sympla is the ticketing platform. Payment can be split into up to 12 instalments, which is common in Brazil. Cancellation rules apply, so read the terms on the Sympla page.

The 2026 price is not published. In 2025 the ticket cost R$20 (about US$4), at the RT rate of 2 October 2026, about R$5.22 per US$. Treat that as a guide only, and check the Sympla page for the final price.

Opening hours and venue

The fair opens on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday from 14:00 to 22:00. On Saturday it opens from 10:00 to 22:00. On Sunday it opens from 10:00, and Sympla gives 21:00 as the closing time, while the fair’s website gives 21:00 as the last entry.

The venue is Expominas, at Avenida Amazonas 6200 in the Gameleira district. Some ticket listings give a different street number, so use the venue’s own address for your taxi or map.

Expominas’s website says the Gameleira Metro station gives access to the venue. Taxis and ride-hailing apps are the alternative.

What to bring

Carry some cash as well as a card, because small stands may have different payment options. Bring a large bag for purchases, and ask sellers about shipping if you buy bulky items.

Foreign visitors should keep their passport copy or residency card with them, in case a card payment needs identity checks.

What else to do in Belo Horizonte that week

The Praça da Liberdade is the city’s cultural centre, with museums around a landscaped square. The Pampulha district has the modernist buildings by Oscar Niemeyer, including a church and an art museum.

Minas Gerais is known for its food, so try pão de queijo and local cheeses. December is the start of the rainy season, so carry an umbrella.

When is the Feira Nacional de Artesanato 2026?

The fair runs from Wednesday 2 to Sunday 6 December 2026 at Expominas in Belo Horizonte.

How much are tickets for the crafts fair?

The 2026 price is not published. In 2025 the ticket cost R$20 (about US$4). Check Sympla for the final price.

What are the opening hours?

Wednesday to Friday 14:00 to 22:00, Saturday 10:00 to 22:00 and Sunday 10:00 to 21:00.

How do I get to Expominas?

Expominas is at Avenida Amazonas 6200 in Gameleira. The venue says the Gameleira Metro station gives access, and taxis are the alternative.

World.title: Soy Luna Final Show Plays Bogotá, Colombia, on 27 October
World.content:
COLOMBIA · MUSIC

Key Facts — What The cast of the Disney series Soy Luna plays El Último Show, billed as the farewell tour.

— When Tuesday 27 October 2026. Doors 18:00, show 21:00. Entry from age 7.

— Where Movistar Arena, Diagonal 61C #26-36, Teusaquillo, Bogotá, Colombia.

— Tickets TuBoleta, COP 329,000 (about US$101) to COP 647,000 (about US$198) in the sections confirmed, fees included, at the RT rate of 2 October 2026 (about COP 3,263 per US$).

— Good to know TransMilenio’s Movistar Arena station is on Avenida NQS. Piso 3 prices may be lower; check TuBoleta.

A show built for families and a generation that grew up with the series, with early doors on a Tuesday.

The cast of Soy Luna plays Movistar Arena in Bogotá, Colombia, on Tuesday 27 October 2026, with doors at 18:00 and the show at 21:00. TuBoleta lists fee-inclusive prices from COP 329,000 (about US$101) to COP 647,000 (about US$198) in the sections we could confirm. Entry starts at age 7.

What Soy Luna is

Soy Luna is a Disney Channel series that ran from 2016 to 2018 for three seasons. It follows a teenager who moves to Buenos Aires and finds a new life on roller skates.

The tour, called El Último Show, is billed as a farewell and marks a return after ten years. The cast includes Karol Sevilla, Michael Ronda, Ruggero Pasquarelli, Malena Ratner and Gastón Vietto. A new season, Soy Luna: Volver, has been announced. No support act is confirmed.

TransMilenio has a Movistar Arena station on Avenida NQS, and the city bus routes 191 and 599 are listed for the area. After a family show, queues at the station are long, so taxis and ride-hailing apps are an alternative.

Check the ticket page for the rules for children before you buy. Bring your passport or residency card for identity checks, and avoid unofficial resale offers.

What else to do in Bogotá that week

La Candelaria, the historic centre, and the Gold Museum are the classic visits.

October is part of the second rainy season, so pack a waterproof layer. Plan the return early, because the show ends late on a Tuesday.

When does Soy Luna play in Bogotá?

The cast plays Movistar Arena on Tuesday 27 October 2026. Doors open at 18:00 and the show starts at 21:00.

How much are Soy Luna tickets in Bogotá?

TuBoleta lists COP 329,000 (about US$101) to COP 647,000 (about US$198) including fees in the sections we confirmed, at about COP 3,263 per US$. Piso 3 may be cheaper.

World.title: Festival Bandera Returns to Rosario on 24 October
World.content:
ARGENTINA · MUSIC

Key Facts — What The seventh Festival Bandera, with four stages and more than 30 acts, led by La Vela Puerca, Dillom and YSY A.

— When Saturday 24 October 2026. Music from 14:30. Doors time not published.

— Where Parque Estación Central Córdoba, 27 de Febrero and Buenos Aires, Rosario, Argentina.

— Tickets Passline, Anticipada Campo ARS 120,000 (about US$79) and Experiencia Bandera ARS 300,000 (about US$197), at the RT rate of 2 October 2026 (about ARS 1,524 per US$). Fees not stated.

— Good to know Visa cards from Banco Santa Fe offer six interest-free instalments. Prices rise with each sales batch.

Rosario’s flagship rock and pop festival moves to a new site this year and adds a fourth stage.

Festival Bandera returns to Rosario, Argentina, on Saturday 24 October 2026 at Parque Estación Central Córdoba. The seventh edition has four stages and more than 30 acts, with music from 14:30. Passline lists Anticipada Campo tickets at ARS 120,000 (about US$79) and Experiencia Bandera at ARS 300,000 (about US$197).

What Festival Bandera is

Festival Bandera is a one-day music festival in Rosario, the Argentine city that celebrates the national flag. The flag was first raised there on 27 February 1812, and the festival takes its name from it.

The seventh edition moves from the Hipódromo to a new site, the Parque Estación Central Córdoba. It also adds a fourth stage, a first for the festival. Local press says more than 25,000 people came last year.

Rosario seen from the Paraná river. File photo. Photo: Maximiliano Kolus, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

The headliners include the Uruguayan band La Vela Puerca, the Argentine rapper Dillom, YSY A and El Mató a un Policía Motorizado. The Colombian band Aterciopelados is also on the bill.

Other acts named by local press are Pastillas del Abuelo, Los Guasones, Peces Raros, Marilina Bertoldi, Javiera Mena from Chile, Zoe Gotusso and Bandalos Chinos. The running order has not been published, so check the festival’s channels closer to the date.

Tickets step by step

Passline is the official seller. The current batch lists Anticipada Campo at ARS 120,000 (about US$79) and Experiencia Bandera, a separate sector, at ARS 300,000 (about US$197). Both prices rose from the first batch, and further increases are possible.

The dollar values use the RT market rate of 2 October 2026, about ARS 1,524 per US$. The sources do not say whether fees are included, so confirm the total at checkout. Passline allows up to six tickets per purchase, and Visa cards from Banco Santa Fe offer six interest-free instalments.

Venue and getting there

Parque Estación Central Córdoba is at 27 de Febrero and Buenos Aires in Rosario. Rosario lies about 300 kilometres north-west of Buenos Aires.

We found no official transport advice for the new site. Taxis and ride-hailing apps are the practical choice, and the return after the last act needs planning. Music starts at 14:30, and a doors time has not been published.

What else to do in Rosario that week

The Monumento a la Bandera on the Paraná riverfront is the city’s landmark. The river promenade is pleasant on a spring afternoon.

October is spring in Rosario, with warm days and cool evenings. Bring a light jacket for the late hours of an outdoor festival.

World.title: DocsMX Documentary Festival Opens in Mexico City 22 Oct
World.content:
MEXICO · FILM

Key Facts — What The 21st DocsMX, Mexico City’s international documentary festival, with 74 films in six sections.

— When Thursday 22 to Saturday 31 October 2026. Screening times are not yet published.

— Where Cineteca Nacional in Coyoacán is confirmed as a venue. The full venue list is not yet published.

— Tickets No festival-wide price is published. The DocsLab forum of 28 to 30 October costs MX$500 (about US$28), or MX$300 (about US$17) for students.

— Good to know Many films are in Spanish. Check the subtitle language for each title.

Ten days of non-fiction film in Mexico City, with a programme in place but prices and venues still to come.

DocsMX, the international documentary festival of Mexico City, runs from Thursday 22 to Saturday 31 October 2026. The 21st edition shows 74 documentaries in six sections. The festival has not yet published a ticket price or a full venue list.

What DocsMX is

DocsMX is the Festival Internacional de Cine Documental de la Ciudad de México. It is an independent platform for documentary film and social impact.

For expats and nomads in Mexico, it is a practical window into Latin American realities. Films cover migration, identity, human rights, history, sport and culture.

The central plaza in Coyoacán, Mexico City. File photo.

The 2026 programme

The official site lists 74 documentaries in six sections. One of them is Hecho en México, which is dedicated to Mexican productions with nine films. It is a good first stop if you want to see how local filmmakers document their own country.

One confirmed screening is El Equipo del Pueblo. Un sueño Atlante, a documentary about the Mexico City football club Atlante. It screens at the Cineteca Nacional on Wednesday 28 and Thursday 29 October. The Wednesday show is at the Río Churubusco site, number 79 in Coyoacán. The Thursday show is at the Avenida México-Coyoacán site, number 389.

The festival gives its date as 22 to 31 October. An older call for entries listed 22 to 30 October, so use the 31 October end date.

Tickets and prices

The festival has not published a single ticket price for the screenings. Prices may differ by venue, and some events may be free, but that is not confirmed. Check docsmx.org and the Cineteca Nacional site for each screening.

The professional forum DocsLab runs from 26 to 30 October. Its seminar days of 28 to 30 October cost MX$500 (about US$28), or MX$300 (about US$17) for students. The conversion uses the RT rate of 2 October 2026, about MX$18.1 per US$.

Venues and getting there

The Cineteca Nacional is in Coyoacán, in the south of Mexico City, and has two addresses used for the festival. Check which address applies to your screening before you travel.

The festival has not published the full venue list. Taxis and ride-hailing apps are easy options in Coyoacán. Many films are in Spanish, so check the subtitle language on the film page.

What else to do in Mexico City that week

Coyoacán has a leafy central plaza, cafés and the Frida Kahlo Museum, which usually needs advance booking. Allow time for a walk between screenings.

October is the end of the rainy season, so carry a light rain jacket. Late October also brings the Day of the Dead preparations, with altars and markets across the city.

When is DocsMX 2026?

DocsMX runs from Thursday 22 to Saturday 31 October 2026 in Mexico City.

How many films are in DocsMX 2026?

The official site lists 74 documentaries in six sections, including nine in the Hecho en México section.

How much are DocsMX tickets?

No festival-wide price is published yet. The DocsLab seminar days cost MX$500 (about US$28), or MX$300 (about US$17) for students.

Where does DocsMX take place?

The Cineteca Nacional in Coyoacán is a confirmed venue. The festival has not yet published the full list of venues.

World.title: Masked men rob woman near Blue Marlin Drive; victim injured during struggle
World.content:
Masked men rob woman near Blue Marlin Drive; victim injured during struggle

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Belize City police are investigating after a woman was reportedly attacked and robbed by two masked men in the Caribbean Shores area on Thursday afternoon.

A 30-year-old woman told police she was walking near the corner of Cottontree/Cotton Wick Street and Blue Marlin Drive at around 1:37 p.m. when two men dressed in black and wearing ski masks approached her from behind near Good Fortune Chinese Shop.

The men allegedly took her black backpack containing approximately $300, a Belize driver’s licence, Social Security card and Atlantic Bank debit card.

Police say a struggle occurred during the robbery, resulting in the woman suffering abrasions to her left wrist and pain to her right shoulder.

The two assailants subsequently fled along Cotton Wick Street. Police investigations continue.

World.title: Rubber Boots Beating: Woman beat by sister-in-law with rubber boots on San Roman banana farm
World.content:
Rubber Boots Beating: Woman beat by sister-in-law with rubber boots on San Roman banana farm

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are seeking a woman following an alleged attack on a banana farm worker in San Roman Village, Stann Creek District, in which the complainant says she was repeatedly struck with a rubber boot.

A 33-year-old woman reported that she returned from work around 7:30 p.m. Thursday and was walking home when her sister-in-law called out to her.

The woman told police that her sister-in-law approached her aggressively, asked, “What is your problem?” and subsequently picked up a black rubber boot and struck her on the forehead.

According to the report, the woman attempted to defend herself but was allegedly struck several more times.

The woman told police she did not know what prompted the confrontation and requested court action.

Police issued her with a medico-legal form and listed the sister-in-law as a wanted person.

World.title: Chad Borland killed, another injured after car plunges 150 feet into bushes off Hummingbird Highway
World.content:
Chad Borland killed, another injured after car plunges 150 feet into bushes off Hummingbird Highway

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a fatal road traffic accident near Belmopan in which a vehicle reportedly left the Hummingbird Highway and travelled approximately 150 feet into thick bushes, leaving one man dead and another injured.

Police received information about the accident around 4:00 p.m. on Thursday, October 1, near La Cabana bar, shortly after Wooden Street.

At the scene, officers encountered Jeffrey Perez with an apparent injury to the back of his head.

Police followed a trail of vehicle debris leading diagonally from the highway into the bushes, where they found a black Mazda extensively damaged and facing away from the highway.

A second man, identified as Chad Borland of University Boulevard, Belmopan, was found motionless approximately one foot away from the vehicle. He was transported to the Western Regional Hospital, where he was pronounced dead at 5:20 p.m.

Preliminary police investigations indicate the Mazda had been travelling from the direction of the roundabout toward Armenia before leaving the roadway.

Police say statements remained to be obtained and surveillance cameras in the vicinity of La Cabana bar were also expected to be reviewed as the investigation continues.

World.title: Toledo man on his way to buy ‘Badman’ at 2 in the morning attacked for $20 with pint bottle
World.content:
Toledo man on his way to buy ‘Badman’ at 2 in the morning attacked for $20 with pint bottle

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are seeking two brothers following an alleged attack in San Felipe Village, Toledo District, in which a 41-year-old man was reportedly wounded with a broken pint bottle after being unable to hand over $20.

Police say they responded to a report of a physical altercation shortly after 2:00 a.m. on Friday and encountered one man suffering injuries to his left ear and the right side of his head.

That man reportedly told police that he had left home between 1:30 and 2:00 a.m. to purchase a “badman” at a village bar when he was confronted by two brothers known to him.

According to the report, the men demanded $20, and when the complainant was unable to produce the money, he was allegedly attacked with a broken pint bottle.

He was taken to the Punta Gorda Community Hospital, where his injuries were certified as wounding. Police say, however, that after being discharged at 5:10 a.m., he declined to provide a formal statement.

The brothers are nevertheless listed by police as wanted in connection with the matter.

World.title: Masked robbers hold up Punta Gorda bar; suspect detained, imitation firearm recovered
World.content:
Masked robbers hold up Punta Gorda bar; suspect detained, imitation firearm recovered

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating an armed robbery at a bar in Punta Gorda Town after two masked men reportedly entered the establishment and made off with cash and other items on Thursday night.

According to police, a bar manager reported that around 10:16 p.m. on October 1, two men entered the establishment on Lucille Melendez Boulevard. One of the men was reportedly armed with what appeared to be a firearm and pointed it at an employee, while his accomplice went into the cashier area and took approximately $400 in cash.

The robbers also allegedly took a pack of cigarettes and an employee’s black and grey bag containing personal documents.

Police say the entire incident lasted approximately three to four minutes before the men escaped through the front door and headed in the direction of a nearby park. Both suspects had their faces and heads covered. No one was injured.

Surveillance footage from inside the establishment reportedly captured the robbery.

Following statements obtained from the manager and two other persons, police conducted a house search and recovered what investigators described as an imitation firearm suspected to have been used in the robbery. A Punta Gorda Town resident was subsequently detained pending investigation.

World.title: Crown seeks life sentence for Krismar Espinosa in execution-style murder of Wilbert Banks Jr.
World.content:
Crown seeks life sentence for Krismar Espinosa in execution-style murder of Wilbert Banks Jr.

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Crown is asking the High Court to impose a life sentence on convicted murderer Krismar Espinosa for the execution-style killing of cyclist and bicycle technician Wilbert “Yellow” Banks Jr., arguing that several aggravating factors make a fixed-term sentence inappropriate.

During mitigation before Justice Nigel Pilgrim, Crown Counsel Maria Nembhard-Santana stressed that Espinosa had previously been convicted of manslaughter in another killing and had only been out of prison for approximately nine months when he was charged with Banks’ murder. The Crown also pointed to the use of a firearm, the seven gunshot wounds suffered by Banks and evidence that the killing had been planned in advance.

Espinosa, meanwhile, declined to personally address the court and called no character witnesses. Through his attorney, he continued to maintain his innocence and relied on a Social Inquiry Report prepared for sentencing.

Justice Pilgrim has reserved sentencing until October 13, 2026. Espinosa remains on remand at the Belize Central Prison.

Banks, 38, was shot seven times on April 5, 2024, in the Lake Garden area near Ladyville. He attempted to drive away after being shot but crashed his vehicle. Police recovered nine 9mm expended shells and a cellphone from the scene.

The prosecution’s key witness was Banks’ former girlfriend, who was Espinosa’s girlfriend at the time. She testified by video link that Espinosa threatened to kill her and her young son unless she lured Banks to the Lake Garden area. She said Banks later drove her there, where Espinosa emerged and opened fire.

Justice Pilgrim found Espinosa guilty of murder on July 31 following a trial without a jury. The court accepted the woman as a credible and reliable witness and rejected Espinosa’s account that he was at home when Banks was killed.

The court also heard emotional victim-impact statements from Banks’ employer Andrew Ordonez, his father Wilbert Banks Sr. and his 14-year-old daughter. His daughter recalled Sunday barbecues, Valentine’s Day gifts and the sense of safety she felt around her father, telling the court that “Father’s Day is no longer the same.”

Banks was well known in Belize’s cycling community and worked at Ordonez Bike Shop. His death was widely mourned after the 2024 killing.

World.title: UNICEF Belize and Special Envoy join forces to promote inclusion of children with disabilities
World.content:
UNICEF Belize and Special Envoy join forces to promote inclusion of children with disabilities

By Zoila Palma: UNICEF Belize and the Special Envoy for the Development of Families and Children have joined forces to promote the rights, inclusion, and well-being of children with disabilities across Belize, under the message: “Every Child Seen. Every Child Heard. Every Child Included.”

The partnership aims to challenge stereotypes, raise awareness, and promote a more inclusive Belize where every child is valued, supported, and empowered to reach their full potential.

The initiative will also amplify the voices of children with disabilities and highlight their strengths, achievements, and contributions.

The partners emphasized that children with disabilities should not be defined by their challenges, noting that they are dreamers, leaders, learners, creators, and changemakers whose stories, voices, and rights matter. The initiative encourages families, schools, communities, and organizations to help create environments where every child can thrive.

Through the partnership, UNICEF Belize and the Special Envoy are calling for greater inclusion and support for children with disabilities, with the goal of making inclusion the norm rather than the exception.

World.title: Government and Global Fund strengthen partnership to support vulnerable Belizeans
World.content:
Government and Global Fund strengthen partnership to support vulnerable Belizeans

By Zoila Palma: The Government of Belize and the Global Fund have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening collaboration and supporting vulnerable populations across the country. The discussions were held between Minister of Economic Transformation Dr. Osmond Martinez and Global Fund Portfolio Manager Marcos Patino Mayer.

Minister Martinez was accompanied by Director Leroy Martinez and Project Manager Ferdy Cabb during the meeting.

Discussions focused on the performance and achievements of Global Fund Cycle 7 being implemented under the Ministry of Economic Transformation, as well as potential funding opportunities and priority areas for Cycle 8.

Minister Martinez expressed appreciation to Patino Mayer and the Global Fund for their continued support to Belize. He highlighted the importance of the organization’s commitment to reaching and supporting some of the country’s most vulnerable populations.

The meeting reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of Belize and the Global Fund to continued partnership and collaboration.

World.title: Hospitals hobbled
World.content:
The Health and Wellness Ministry says there were no adverse events at the island’s public health facilities Friday after junior doctors stayed away in protest over a long-running dispute with the Government relating to overtime pay.

However, checks by Jamaica Observer journalists in rural areas found long wait times at some facilities, while others showed no evidence of outpatient activity.

World.title: Triggerman gets life sentence for murder of Paulwell’s daughter and her mother
World.content:
Toshyna Patterson and her daughter Serayah Paulwell were kidnapped and murdered in September 2023.

David Smith, the triggerman in the murder of Member of Parliament Phillip Paulwell’s 10-month-old daughter, Sarayah, and her mother, Toshyna Patterson, has been sentenced to life in prison for the crime.

The Kingston-based painter is to serve a minimum of 45 years behind bars before becoming eligible for parole.

The sentencing was handed down by Chief Justice Bryan Sykes on Friday under a reported plea deal.

Smith was among a number of persons charged in the double murder which rocked the nation.

Patterson and her daughter were reported missing on September 9, 2023. Prosecutors say the mother and daughter were taken to Warieka Hills in St Andrew where they were shot and killed and their bodies burnt.

The alleged mastermind behind the killing, former United States Navy culinary specialist Leoda Bradshaw is charged with two counts of conspiracy to murder, two counts of conspiracy to kidnapping, two counts of kidnapping, and two counts of capital murder.

World.title: Gov’t says its committed to fair resolution in doctors pay dispute
World.content:
In this file photo Minister of Labour and Social Security, Pearnel Charles Jr, speaking during a post-Cabinet press briefing.

Government says its “committed to a fair, lawful and peaceful resolution” to the standoff over overtime pay that has led to junior doctors taking industrial action on Friday.

READ: Brace for delays in health services, JMDA warns amid pay dispute

In a release on Friday, the Minister of Labour and Social Security said it acknowledges the concerns of members of the Jamaica Medical Doctors’ Association (JMDA) as they await the Industrial Disputes Tribunal’s award in the dispute between the association and the Government of Jamaica.

The matter is before the IDT for compulsory arbitration under the Labour Relations and Industrial Disputes Act.

The ministry said the tribunal must be allowed to carry out its functions independently.

Accordingly, the release stated, the minister and the ministry will refrain from commenting on the merits of the dispute or taking any action that could be construed as seeking to influence the tribunal’s decision.

“Our medical doctors provide an invaluable service to Jamaica. Their dedication and sacrifice deserve recognition, and the ministry understands the importance of a timely resolution to these longstanding matters,” it said. “The Government remains committed to a fair, lawful and peaceful resolution and has confidence in the Tribunal’s consideration of the evidence and the issues before it.”

The ministry said it encourages all parties to maintain constructive engagement and industrial harmony while the proceedings are concluded.

“A timely resolution, consistent with due process, remains important to our doctors, the healthcare system and the public we all serve,” the ministry said.

World.title: WATCH: Mandeville Regional in emergency mode amid junior doctors strike
World.content:
MANCHESTER, Jamaica — Senior Medical Officer at the Mandeville Regional Hospital Dr Everton McIntosh is appealing to medical doctors to assist in manning the facility where junior doctors are currently on strike.

“I just want to make an appeal, so if there are any doctors out there who are willing to do some sessions at the hospital, we are inviting persons to come forward… especially for the emergency departments. We would appreciate the assistance,” he told journalists Friday morning.

READ: Brace for delays in health services, JMDA warns amid pay dispute

The doctors on strike are protesting what they say is the slow pace of the review process by the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to hand down a ruling as it relates to overtime payments.

Dr McIntosh said over 100 junior doctors have stayed off the job with about 24 consultants manning all the wards and departments at the regional facility.

“We should have a total of 133 doctors on duty, but just the consultants are here which is around 24 who are working, so you can see the discrepancy there, out of a total of 133. That has grave implications for the ability for us to cover all of the areas adequately in terms of the wards, the emergency department, the outpatient clinics,” he said while pointing out that there are 315 patients admitted at the hospital as of Friday morning.

— Kasey Williams

World.title: Dad vs son in clash of Butlers
World.content:
Craig Butler (left) and Kyle Butler

KINGSTON, Jamaica — For 90 minutes on Saturday, football will pit father against son when Mona High technical director Craig Butler comes face-to-face with Vauxhall High coach, his son Kyle Butler in an intriguing ISSA Walker Cup quarterfinal.

But while Craig will be desperate to see Mona advance, the veteran football developer admits there would be something special about watching his son lift the Walker Cup with Vauxhall.

Craig, who has spent years nurturing young Jamaican footballers through his Phoenix Academy, said his ultimate wish is for Kyle and his daughter Kaycie to surpass his own achievements.

“I have raised Kyle and Kaycie to surpass my achievements. Only a father who doesn’t love his children would want them not to succeed,” Craig said.

The father-son showdown — set for 2pm at Waterhouse stadium — is an unusual twist to what is already one of the more intriguing Walker Cup quarterfinals, but Craig believes football has provided the family with a unique opportunity to work together, travel and share memorable moments.

“In football, we have an opportunity as a family to work and to spend valuable time and banter,” he said.

Craig has travelled extensively during his football career, taking Jamaican football talent to various parts of the world.

He recently pointed to the progress of Phoenix graduate Daniel Scarlett, who has signed with Australian club Central Coast Mariners, as another example of the opportunities available to young local players.

But on Saturday, the focus will be squarely on Mona and Vauxhall.

Craig has been impressed with the transformation of Vauxhall under Kyle and believes his son has earned the respect of the school community.

“It would be wonderful for Kyle to win the Walker Cup and Manning Cup with Vauxhall. He is well loved there and has done wonders with the school and the players,” he said.

However, Craig knows Kyle faces a major obstacle in Mona, who have developed a football identity over several years.

“Mona is in another mode now. They have ascended with a team built over the last six years,” he said.

“It is a brand of football that is embedded in the school and its players, and it will be hard,” Craig added.

There is also a strong Phoenix connection between the two teams, making Saturday’s contest even more significant for the Butler family.

Craig, however, is not allowing the rivalry to overshadow the bigger picture.

“Both teams are Phoenix and, either way it goes, it will be love again after the game,” he said.

And that sentiment is likely to define the Butler family story long after the final whistle — regardless of whether father Craig or son Kyle is celebrating a place in the Walker Cup semi-finals.

– Howard Walker

World.title: Senior doctors pick up the slack in western region
World.content:
Cornwall Regional Hospital

ST JAMES, Jamaica — Clinical Coordinator for the Western Regional Health Authority (WRHA), Dr Delroy Fray, is seeking to reassure the public that contingency measures are in place to minimise any disruption caused by industrial action taken by doctors.

The doctors are protesting what they say is the slow pace of the review process by the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to hand down a ruling as it relates to overtime payments.

“We’ve made contingency plans so that our urgent and emergency cases will not be compromised in any way,” Fray told Observer Online on Friday morning.

“We knew what would happen today so yesterday was a planning day for us and the plan was to have our senior doctors cover the gaps,” he said.

The Western Region has four major health care facilities which includes the Cornwall Regional Hospital and Fray said that since 8:00am on Friday, the senior doctors have taken action.

However, he said that they are managing based on the plans put in place.

“I have checked in the morning and we are moving along that line very well. I am going to be monitoring that every four hours to see what the flow is like and how we are coping,” he said.

“Based on the plans I have in place for all the four hospitals, I’m not worried, I think we should be alright and the fact that it is just 24 hours, I think we can manage,” he added.

It was reported that the Noel Holmes hospital in Lucea currently has five doctors on staff which would have normally been nine.

World.title: Brace for delays in health services, JMDA warns amid pay dispute
World.content:
Doctors say if there is no ruling in their wage dispute with the Government by Friday, October 2, 2026, they cannot guarantee normalcy within the health sector across the island (Photo: Adobe Stock)

Jamaicans have been warned to brace for longer wait times and delays in the completion of procedures in the healthcare sector as junior doctors remain restive over the matter of overtime rates which has been before the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) for the past year.

In a press release on Friday, Jamaica Medical Doctors Association (JMDA) President Dr Jubilee Brown said the body “cannot guarantee normalcy from 8 am on Friday, October 2, 2026 to 8 am on Saturday, October 3, 2026.

“Only emergency services will be provided during this period,” the JMDA president said.

She added that the association has activated relevant protocols to minimise adverse outcomes during the period.

According to the JMDA, the Government owes the doctors $31 billion in retroactive overtime, but the Government’s calculation sits at $23 billion.

“We have been working at the same overtime rates since 2021. This is unacceptable. The JMDA calls upon the Industrial Disputes Tribunal to hand down its award without further delay,” Brown said.

World.title: No fallout
World.content:
The scene in Black River in the immediate aftermath of Hurricane Melissa last October. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

DESPITE concerns from some quarters over the slow spending of Hurricane Melissa donations, permanent secretary in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Sheila Sealy Monteith says the Jamaican Diaspora has not raised any complaints about how its contributions are being used.

Sealy Monteith told Parliament’s Internal and External Affairs Committee on Thursday that the ministry had “many opportunities” to receive feedback from the Diaspora but had not received any indication of concern. The assurance came against the backdrop of concerns about the pace at which millions of dollars donated following Hurricane

Melissa have been utilised. Category 5 Melissa left immense damage after slamming into Jamaica’ south-western coast on October 28, 2025 and swept across western and north-western parishes.

During the committee’s deliberations with the ministry, Opposition Member of Parliament Dr Kenneth Russell raised the Auditor General’s finding that only about 1.7 per cent of the donated funds had been used months after the contributions were made.

“Has the ministry, one, received any feedback from the members of the Diaspora and the donors about the slow use of their contributions? And secondly, is the ministry concerned about the reputational risks done to the country and the effect it will have on your ability to raise funds should a similar situation recur?”

Russell queried.

Sealy Monteith responded that the ministry had not seen evidence of a decline in confidence in Jamaica’s ability to handle international support.

“We have used the strength of our diplomacy to ensure that countries who wish to contribute are enabled to contribute, that we are able to record it. We are providing direction for them, and we pass them on to the relevant authorities.

We have not received any indication to date that there has been a loss of confidence in our abilities to use it,” she revealed.

The permanent secretary stressed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade’s role is primarily to facilitate international assistance, rather than to determine how the funds are ultimately spent.

She said the ministry works with other government entities to ensure that countries and other contributors wishing to assist Jamaica are able to do so and are directed to the relevant authorities.

Sealy Monteith also suggested that the pace at which contributions are absorbed and deployed must be considered in the context of the capacity of the receiving authorities to use the support.

“I think people understand also that when support comes in, it requires the ability to be able to assimilate and to use, and that comes over time as well,” she said. “So, if you’re asking me whether there’s been a fallout of interest and solidarity, I have not seen that. We continue to be a preferred guest on many agendas, and Minister [Kamina Johnson Smith] had a schedule in New York last week that was head-turning because everybody wants Jamaica to be at the table, to sit on our committees, to be there,” she added

World.title: Sandu slams Russia as attack debris hits Moldova in latest airspace violation
World.content:
Moldova's President Maia Sandu reacts during the Coalition of the Willing meeting, in Kyiv on August 24, 2026. | Tetiana Dzhafarova/AFP via Getty Images

Three missile and two drones entered Moldovan airspace and caused collateral damage in the country, local authorities said.

Moldovan President Maia Sandu on Saturday hit out at Moscow after saying debris from five Russian air attack weapons violated the country’s airspace and exploded on the country’s territory.

“I condemn Russia’s attack on Ukraine this morning. Its war is dangerously reaching Moldova,” she wrote on X. “Russian air attack weapons, including Banderol missiles and drones, violated our airspace and exploded on our soil.”

In all, three missiles and two drones flew over the country between 7.45 a.m. and 8 a.m., with fragments later found in the country’s eastern districts of Hincesti, Anenii Noi and Causeni. The police were dispatched to secure the debris, which caused a fire to break out but no casualties.

World.title: Russia hits major Kyiv bridge, logistics hub in latest attack
World.content:
Russia’s defense ministry confirmed it had carried out the attack, stating the bridge was being used to transport military cargo. It also separately said it had struck the key Hostomel logistics hub and a cargo ship crossing the Black Sea near the southern port of Odessa.

Separately, the UN-linked International Atomic Energy Agency said four strikes in recent days had threatened safety and security” at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, including reportedly disabling an off-site radiation monitoring station.

Moscow has stepped up its bombing campaign in recent weeks against Ukraine’s civil and critical infrastructure, targeting residential areas, energy facilities, sea terminals and data centers, setting the stage for a dire winter for Kyiv. In the past week alone, Russia has launched more than 190 missiles and drones, mostly targeting energy infrastructure.

The Russian foreign affairs ministry issued a statement on Saturday warning “foreign nationals and diplomatic personnel against remaining in” Kyiv.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered his troops to abandon the rules of war, Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the FT this week.

Meanwhile, Ukraine is grappling with a yawning financial deficit and shortage of critical weapons. Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi this week said the country faces a $27 billion defense funding gap this year, with Kyiv hoping to cover about $7 billion domestically and looking to partners for the rest.

This article was updated.

World.title: Widdecombe murder suspect charged with planning terror act on Nigel Farage
World.content:
Britain’s head of counter-terrorism policing Vicki Evans said the force had “been running a hugely intensive and complex investigation for some time,” adding: “The charge announced today is a result of the tireless work of investigators across the counter-terrorism policing network.”

Kerry is set to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday.

In August, the counter-terrorism force reopened a year-long investigation into an alleged firebomb attack against Farage’s home.

“I know the new charges made today will be extremely concerning. My profound sympathies are with Nigel Farage and his family,” said British Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. “Let no one make any mistake: an attack on anyone in politics is an attack on us all.”

A Reform official told the BBC: “This is exactly why Nigel needed £5m to protect his security for life.”

Farage is facing a parliamentary watchdog probe into a £5m gift from a billionaire donor before he became an MP in 2024, previously claiming he needed the money to ensure his security.

World.title: Wie Russland die NATO provoziert. Mit Carlo Masala
World.content:
Eine Drohne mit Sprengstoff an einer ukrainischen Frachtmaschine in Leipzig, Explosionen in Munitionsfabriken und Sabotage auf See. Russland intensiviert seine hybride Kriegsführung mitten in Europa und testet gezielt die roten Linien der NATO. Doch was passiert, wenn ein solcher Anschlag auf deutschem Boden tatsächlich gelingt und den Bündnisfall auslöst? Darüber spricht Gordon Repinski in dieser Folge mit Carlo Masala, Professor für Internationale Politik, Universität der Bundeswehr München.

Das Ziel des Kremls ist es, Panik zu schüren und die westliche Unterstützung für die Ukraine zu brechen. Im Gespräch analysiert Carlo, warum Putin gerade jetzt risikofreudiger wird und weshalb Friedrich Merz in der deutschen Debatte als entscheidender Schutzwall für weitere Hilfen gilt. Ein Wegbrechen dieser Unterstützung hätte fatale finanzielle und militärische Folgen für den gesamten Kontinent.

Gleichzeitig wächst der Druck auf Kiew massiv. Die Episode beleuchtet, wie eine mögliche Rückkehr von Trump ins Weiße Haus die Ukraine zu schmerzhaften Deals zwingen könnte und warum das europäische Superwahljahr 2027 Moskau eine beispiellose Chance bietet, die politische Landschaft endgültig zu seinen Gunsten zu drehen.

World.title: Latvian PM faces bittersweet victory in election backdropped by Russia
World.content:
His center-right partners, New Unity, are struggling to cross the 5% electoral threshold, which would be a floundering performance for a party that has been home to many Latvian prime ministers, including current European Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis.

But for the party’s prime ministerial candidate and ex-Finance Minister Arvils Ašeradens, the low polling numbers are simply the “political pendulum which shifts from one way to the other,” he told POLITICO in Riga last month.

During the last election in 2022, New Unity was the major beneficiary of a rally-round-the-flag moment as Russia had just launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. But in 2026, voters seem frustrated with Latvia’s high inflation, the ongoing uncertainty surrounding national airline airBaltic and instrumentalized migration orchestrated by Russia and Belarus.

The prime minister may need to open talks with Ainārs Šlesers, a right-wing veteran of Latvian politics. | Robert Hegedus/EPA

Kulbergs’ other coalition partner, the agrarian Union of Greens and Farmers (known as ZZS), is also polling below the threshold. And if neither party manages to scrape by, it might force Kulbergs to work with the controversial businessman Šlesers, who carefully advocated expanding trade with Russia.

Kulbergs has dismissed this possibility — “as it is given now: no,” he told POLITICO in early September — because he does not trust the people Šlesers has surrounded himself with. Just weeks earlier, however, he had been less definitive, telling POLITICO in July: “I have to see what chess pieces I will get … to make a coalition.”

Šlesers has been a central figure in Latvian politics for decades, most notably as a local “oligarch” who, via family holdings, exerts influence over the Port of Riga. The capital’s harbor has seen its largely Russian and Belarusian hinterland slowly carved off by EU sanctions. And after Kulbergs slapped 300% tariffs on transited Russian grain this month , Šlesers told Latvian national TV such transit should be allowed, though he supports Ukraine’s EU accession.

World.title: ‘Maxi merde’: French presidential campaign rattled by a week of chaos
World.content:
Though that individual, who was granted anonymity to candidly discuss the current situation, was only referring to the increasingly violent demonstrations outside secondary schools and the government’s slow-footed response to them, it’s a sentiment likely shared by French voters after a week of particularly bleak headlines.

If there are political winners, it’s not immediately clear who they are. Establishment candidates and moderate voices are still struggling to seize the narrative from far-right presidential front-runner Marine Le Pen and her surging far-left challenger Jean-Luc Mélenchon — both of whom want to fundamentally reshape France and its relationship with Europe.

A survey by pollster Odoxa this week found that the French disapprove of the government’s handling of the student school protests, but they also disapprove of Mélenchon and his far-left party France Unbowed’s involvement.

Mélenchon’s allies have joined demonstrators outside schools, saying they were there to show support and protect minors from confrontations with police. But the government and France Unbowed’s political opponents accuse them of fanning the flames of violence — allegations they deny.

“There’s a battle over the narrative” between the political extremes, a Socialist Party adviser said.

Whatever the case, the week’s crises are showing just how nasty the campaign can get with two populist candidates unafraid to stoke partisan divisions leading the polls.

World.title: Polanski’s Greens look for their next opening
World.content:
Polanski added: “Through our sustained pressure — and our historic wins — we have held the worst instincts of the Labour government in check. And started to move them in the right direction.”

The Labour washout in May’s local elections, courtesy of voter defections to right-wing populist Reform UK as well as to the Greens, accelerated Starmer’s exit as prime minister over the summer. Burnham has since promised many of the things that under Starmer were within the Greens’ sole purview — public ownership, care, and housing.

The task for the Green leader now is to decide where to push Labour next.

“It won’t surprise you to hear that I’m not hopeful about Labour’s backbone,” he told the crowd.

Hackney Mayor Zoë Garbett, who won her job in May’s local elections, said there were still “key differences” with the governing party, particularly on Gaza, climate and rent control — but conceded that Burnham had made it more difficult for the Green message.

She said: “People were so fed up in May, they were done with people making promises and not delivering, but we need to put forward what our vision is as well, that’s what this conference and Zack’s speech is about.”

World.title: 17 countries join forces to oppose EU budget cuts
World.content:
"We therefore believe that the overall funding for Cohesion Policy and the CAP must be preserved in the next MFF," the seventeen countries wrote in the letter to Irish Taoiseach Micheal Martin seen by POLITICO.

The signatories include Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Romanian President Nicușor Dan coordinated the initiative and will host an informal meeting of those countries in the margins of the next European Council on Oct. 15 and 16.

The Multiannual Financial Framework, or MFF, finances everything from farmers’ subsidies to development aid, and is among the toughest negotiations in Brussels. In 2025, the European Commission proposed a budget of nearly €2 trillion for the 2028-2034 period and shifted hundreds of billions from agriculture and regional payouts, known as cohesion policy, to new priorities such as defense and competitiveness.

The so-called Friends of Cohesion group warned that further reductions to agricultural and cohesion "would only weaken it [budget] and risk undermining public support for the European project."

Ireland’s negotiating document, or negobox, will set the scene for discussions among the EU’s 27 leaders during the summit in Brussels in October.

World.title: Showers and storms across Spain this weekend, floods kill 102-year-old woman
World.content:
A 102-year-old woman died and 90 people had to be rescued on Friday in Madrigueras, in the province of Albacete, after flash flooding swamped the entire town.

 

According to a statement from the regional government, the municipality recorded 142 litres of rain per square metre, a level that forced the deployment of a large emergency operation. The regional authorities also activated the Adverse Meteorological Risk Plan (METEOCAM) at operational level 1.

In the house where the victim was found, the water reached a height of one metre. During the afternoon and the early part of the night, emergency services carried out around 90 rescues, mostly of people in homes affected by the build-up of water. The regional government said it had received numerous calls from residents who "were frightened and did not know how to act".

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez expressed his support on X. "All my love to the relatives of the woman who has died as a result of the flooding, and all our support and solidarity to the affected residents," he wrote. The president of Castilla-La Mancha, Emiliano García-Page, is in Madrigueras on Saturday, where the Civil Guard is working on clean-up operations.

Storms over the weekend

Heavy rain fell during the night and on Friday morning in Tarragona and Castellón, especially in the Lower Ebro area, where most of the problems were concentrated. On Friday afternoon, orange alerts were in place in Tarragona, the Valencia region and the Balearic Islands, and also in the Region of Murcia and in the provinces of Almería, Granada and Albacete, for storms that could be strong and bring hail. The unsettled weather is spreading to more areas of the peninsula and will continue throughout the weekend.

Saturday may start with further heavy rain along the Tarragona coast, where a red alert has already been issued for torrential rain, as well as in Extremadura, Salamanca, the Central System and Aragon. From midday, and especially in the afternoon, showers and thunderstorms could reach virtually any part of the peninsula.

They will again be intense and accompanied by hail in some places, namely the Iberian System, the south-eastern sierras, the Pyrenees, the north-western quadrant, the Balearic Islands and the Mediterranean coast. They will be less likely in western Galicia and in the Canary Islands. Temperatures will rise in Galicia, Aragon, Navarre, the Basque Country and the Canary Islands, fall in Catalonia, the Balearic Islands and inland Spain, and remain unchanged elsewhere.

On Sunday, the unsettled conditions will continue, with widespread rain and thunderstorms and the possible formation of a DANA, a slow-moving high-altitude low that can bring torrential rain over the western half of mainland Spain. This does not mean that the rainfall will be heavier than in recent hours in Tarragona or Castellón, but it does make it more likely that these conditions will be repeated or spread to other areas. Only along the Galician coast are largely clear or slightly cloudy skies expected.

During the early hours, showers and storms could be heavy along the Cantabrian coast, in the Balearic Islands and in Catalonia. Later, locally heavy showers will become widespread across much of central and northern Spain, and will be less likely in the southern third. The Canary Islands will remain largely unaffected. Temperatures will change little compared with Saturday, with the weekend still feeling warm.

World.title: Greece will not 'borrow' its own treasures, Mitsotakis says of Parthenon Marbles
World.content:
Speaking in Thessaloniki, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis made special reference to the Parthenon Sculptures on the occasion of the exchange of historic relics between Greece and Bulgaria.

 

"Monuments and historic artefacts cannot be treated as spoils of war, nor as victims of circumstances that arose after their creation and their inherent nature as unified works," Mitsotakis said.

"It is precisely this same principle, the principle of a monument's integrity, that underpins our ongoing effort to reunite the Parthenon Sculptures. Because they are not lifeless objects from the past. They are evidence in a living and unbroken connection with the natural and cultural landscape that gave birth to them," the Greek prime minister added.

"The Parthenon is a unique and self-contained case. That is why it cannot be 'imprisoned' within the confines of legal or technical issues. It is about restoring the aesthetic and semantic integrity of a truly universal monument which, unfortunately, remains violently dismembered.

"My country will not accept arrangements that imply recognition of foreign ownership, nor will it borrow, supposedly, its own treasures. On the contrary, it now believes that the time has come for truth, for reason, for justice, but also for morality," Mitsotakis concluded, speaking at the Museum of Byzantine Culture.

Radev: We have left the shadows of the past behind us

"Our joint efforts have allowed us to leave the shadows of the past behind us and to create a relationship of mutual respect and friendship," Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev stressed in his speech at the event.

"I am pleased that our two peoples have managed to move beyond confrontation and today we enjoy a very high level of economic, political and cultural co-operation," he said, adding: "I am full of hope that what we have achieved today will further consolidate our strategic partnership, because over the past decades we have managed to create a very strong axis of strategic co-operation between Bulgaria and Greece, an axis of stability, security, prosperity and development."

The remains of Tsar Samuel

More than a thousand years after his death, the remains identified as those of Tsar Samuel, one of the most important rulers of the First Bulgarian Empire, are returning to Bulgaria. Their return is part of the agreement on the mutual handover of historic artefacts and anthropological material signed by Greece and Bulgaria, which the Bulgarian side has described as being of historic significance.

In exchange, Greece is receiving 48 ecclesiastical artefacts that were removed by Bulgarian troops from churches and monasteries in northern Greece during the First World War. The objects were taken away in 1917 and for more than a century remained in Bulgaria, where they were kept or displayed at the National History Museum in Sofia.

The remains of Tsar Samuel (997-1014), during the protocol-signing ceremony ΑΠΕ-ΜΠΕ/ΑΠΕ-ΜΠΕ/ΑΧΙΛΛΕΑΣ ΧΗΡΑΣ

Samuel ruled from 997 to 1014 and played a leading role in the military clashes with the Byzantine Empire. Initially, he acted together with his brothers, one of whom he later ordered to be executed. Gradually, he extended his authority over a large part of the Balkans, while the region of the Prespa and Ohrid lakes, mainly in what is now North Macedonia, became the centre of his power.

From the early 11th century, however, the situation began to change in favour of the Byzantines. After 1001, the forces of Emperor Basil II intensified their pressure and in 1014 Samuel's army suffered a heavy defeat. According to historical sources, the Byzantine emperor, who became known as "Boulgaroktonos", ordered thousands of Bulgarian prisoners to be blinded. Tradition holds that Samuel suffered a shock when he saw his soldiers returning blind and died shortly afterwards.

The Bulgarian state finally came under Byzantine rule four years after his death, in 1018.

The remains attributed to Samuel are linked to excavations at the Basilica of Saint Achilleios in Prespa. In 1965, Professor Nikolaos Moutsopoulos uncovered four sarcophagi, together with anthropological material. In recent years, the finds have been kept at the Museum of Byzantine Culture in Thessaloniki and now form part of the exchange agreement with Bulgaria.

What Greece is receiving

On the Greek side, the 48 artefacts come from the Holy Monastery of Panagia Eikosifoinissa, the Holy Monastery of Timios Prodromos of Serres and the Holy Metropolis of Serres and Nigrita. Before their final return to the places from which they were removed, they will be on display at the Museum of Byzantine Culture until 5 November 2026.

Ecclesiastical artefacts returning to Greece on display at the Museum of Byzantine Culture ΑΠΕ-ΜΠΕ/ΑΠΕ-ΜΠΕ/ΑΧΙΛΛΕΑΣ ΧΗΡΑΣ

The mutual handover took place on Saturday morning in Thessaloniki, in the presence of Mitsotakis and Radev, with the signing of the relevant delivery and receipt protocols.

The procedure marks the implementation of the memorandum of understanding signed by the culture ministers of Greece and Bulgaria, Lina Mendoni and Eftim Miloshev, after many years of negotiations and regular contacts between the two sides.

World.title: Germany marks 36 years of unity: Why was the country divided and how united is it today?
World.content:
Germany is marking the 36th anniversary of reunification. On 3 October 1990 the former GDR acceded to the Federal Republic, ending a division that had lasted 41 years and making Berlin once again the capital of a united Germany.

 

In Brandenburg, Steeven Bretz, the leader of the Christian Democratic Union in the state parliament, paid tribute to former Chancellor Helmut Kohl at the Glienicke Bridge in Potsdam, where the border once ran. "We owe him a great deal, above all the fact that unity succeeded," Bretz said, according to his Instagram account. "The fact that we are able to celebrate unity is, I believe, a gift of history."

The bridge, which links Berlin and Potsdam, was blown up in the final year of the Second World War, rebuilt and reopened in 1949 as the "Bridge of Unity". It became famous during the Cold War as a site of international exchanges of agents. Brandenburg's state government, led by Minister-President Dietmar Woidke (SPD), is taking part in the main national celebrations in Bremen.

"A dream will come true"

Kohl, whose term of office ran from 1982 to 1998, is regarded as the "chancellor of unity". In a televised address on 2 October 1990, he said: "In a few hours a dream will come true. After more than forty bitter years of division, Germany, our fatherland, is reunited."

He urged Germans to remember those who had suffered under division. "Families were cruelly torn apart. Political prisoners were locked away in jails. People died at the Wall," he said. He also thanked the East Germans who had fought for their freedom, the former victorious powers and the freedom movements in Central, Eastern and Southern Europe.

German reunification is celebrating its 36th anniversary. On 3 October 1990 the former GDR acceded to the Federal Republic. The date also marks the end of the division of Germany, which had lasted a full 41 years.

How united are Germans today?

The 2026 report by the Federal Government Commissioner for Eastern Germany finds that East and West Germans now assess their living conditions similarly in many respects. Nevertheless, East Germans remain under-represented in senior positions in the top federal authorities, although their share has risen from 13.9 to 16.3 percent since 2022.

The difference is particularly striking in inheritances and gifts: in 2025, 95 percent of the total value of taxable transfers of assets accrued to West Germany, according to the Federal Statistical Office.

One reason lies in the upheaval that followed reunification. Only 17 percent of former GDR citizens kept their job after the change of system, according to a study by the Rockwool Foundation Berlin made available in advance to Reuters. Many companies in the former GDR lost their markets or were closed in the 1990s, while young and well-qualified people moved west. As a result, some regions still lack both population and corporate headquarters.

The federal government is trying to reduce these disparities further, focusing support on structurally weak regions.

Why Germany was divided

After the Second World War, the four victorious powers, the USA, the Soviet Union, Great Britain and France, divided defeated Germany into four occupation zones. Against the backdrop of the emerging Cold War, a conflict developed over the country's political and economic future, and in 1949 the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG) was established in the West and the GDR in the East.

Dresden, Saxony: many young people from eastern Germany move to western Germany and abroad. AP Photo

Both were granted sovereignty in 1955, West Germany by the Allies and East Germany by the Soviet Union, but the non-German powers retained special rights. Those rights ended with reunification, the foreign-policy conditions for which were laid down in the Two Plus Four Treaty. In it, the FRG and the GDR recognised the Oder-Neisse line as the border with Poland.

Why 3 October, not 9 November

The Wall fell on 9 November 1989, and that date was initially discussed as a possible national holiday. However, in view of the Reich Pogrom Night of 1938, the decision went against it. The choice fell instead on 3 October 1990, the day the Unification Treaty was implemented.

The day after the fall of the Wall, Berliners danced on top of it to celebrate the end of the inner-German border. (Archive: 10 November 1989) AP Photo

The treaty, signed on 31 August 1990 by FRG Interior Minister Wolfgang Schäuble and GDR State Secretary Günther Krause, both of the CDU, designated 3 October as the "Day of German Unity" and a public holiday. It replaced 17 June, which commemorated the 1953 popular uprising in the GDR and remains a national day of remembrance.

World.title: Seventeen EU leaders press Irish presidency to protect farm funding in next budget
World.content:
The leaders of 17 European Union countries have sent a letter to Taoiseach Micheál Martin, in his capacity as current president-in-office of the Council of the European Union, calling for agriculture to be given priority ahead of the revision of the Negotiating Box, the document drawn up by the presidency to steer and progressively narrow down negotiations on the EU's long-term budget.

 

As negotiations on the 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) enter a decisive phase, the leaders of Bulgaria, Cyprus, Croatia, Estonia, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, the Czech Republic, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain and Hungary have sent "some reflections ahead of the forthcoming revision of the Negotiating Box".

"We fully recognise that the European Union is facing an evolving strategic environment, which brings with it new challenges but also new opportunities for joint European action," reads the letter, whose first signatories are Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Romanian President Nicușor Dan.

"The next MFF must enable Europe to seize these opportunities while at the same time responding to growing challenges, including security and defence, competitiveness, connectivity, energy security and resilience. At the same time, this must not come at the expense of treaty-based policies, which remain the backbone of European integration and themselves help to address these new challenges," the European leaders write.

"Therefore, the overall volume set out in the Negotiating Box of the Cypriot presidency remains the relevant basis for dealing effectively with all these financing needs. This is not the time for Europe to lower its ambitions," the heads of state and government add.

The leaders go on to stress that cohesion policy and the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) are long-standing policies, but that their objectives are more relevant than ever. "They promote convergence between member states and regions, strengthen the single market and support rural and less developed areas. They also contribute to Europe's competitiveness and food security, while providing tangible support to millions of European citizens and demonstrating the added value of common European spending."

In their view, both policies have repeatedly adapted to new economic and social realities while remaining true to their treaty objectives. They also generate direct and indirect benefits for the economies of the entire European Union.

"We therefore believe that overall funding for cohesion policy and the CAP should be preserved in the next MFF. As underlined in our Joint Declaration of 26 May, these policies are already facing real-terms cuts under the Commission's proposal, despite the overall increase in the size of the MFF. A further reduction would not modernise the EU budget; it would merely weaken it and risk undermining public support for the European project. Moreover, the new MFF already entails a fundamental transformation of its structure, programming and spending approach," they explain.

The leaders also argue that Europe's new priorities require appropriate additional resources, while funding for agriculture and cohesion must be safeguarded.

They also say they are ready to work constructively on the revenue side, including on proposals for new own resources that would ease the direct pressure on national budgets. "Such resources should be genuine, fair, simple and non-regressive, in line with our May declaration. We will carefully assess the adjustments to the proposals that the Commission has committed to present," the letter continues.

According to the leaders of the 17 signatory countries, options that should be considered include a more gradual repayment of NextGenerationEU, which could create additional fiscal space in the next MFF, subject to an assessment of its impact on the overall cost of repayment, as well as limited and targeted European debt instruments for clearly identified strategic priorities, in line with the May declaration.

For the leaders, the current system of rebates should have no place in the next MFF. The rebates were intended to address an excessive burden on the contributions of certain member states. The circumstances that originally justified these corrections, they argue, have fundamentally changed. When assessing national contributions, account should be taken not only of their absolute level but also of the differing levels of prosperity of the member states and the relative effort required of each of them, the leaders conclude, saying they remain open to working with the Council presidency.

World.title: China opens anti-dumping probe into EU days before Beijing trade talks
World.content:
China has opened an anti-dumping investigation into a chemical imported from the European Union, less than a week before the bloc's trade commissioner arrives in Beijing for talks meant to stop a dispute from escalating.

 

The commerce ministry in China said on Saturday it would examine whether low-priced p-nitrotoluene from the EU was flooding the Chinese market. A spokesperson said domestic producers had asked for the probe, complaining of "damage to production and operations".

The chemical is used to make dyes, pharmaceuticals and pesticides and the investigation is due to conclude within 12 months, with a possible six-month extension.

It follows an investigation by the EU, opened in September, into polyvinyl chloride imports from countries including China. Beijing denies that its manufacturers owe their competitiveness to state support and has threatened countermeasures against EU moves to block its firms.

"China has repeatedly reiterated that the EU needs to face its own economic and trade problems directly and resolve mutual concerns through dialogue and consultation," the spokesperson said.

What is dumping?

Dumping is when a company exports a product for less than it charges at home, or for less than it costs to make. World Trade Organization rules allow the importing country to respond with extra tariffs, known as anti-dumping duties, if an investigation finds that the cheap imports have injured its own producers.

Brussels is reaching for the tool far more often. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in August that the EU had opened 30 trade defence investigations in a year, nearly triple the usual rate, as Chinese imports rose 45% in five years.

Sefčovič heads to Beijing

EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Sefčovič will be in Beijing on 8–9 October to co-chair a session of the EU-China Trade and Investment Council and meet Commerce Minister Wang Wentao. The visit marks the deadline Brussels set in June for the first tangible results from its dialogue with Beijing.

Brussels wants assurances that China will curb exports to the EU and extend a truce on rare earth exports, with the bloc's trade deficit running at €1 billion a day. Beijing has already warned it would respond firmly to any new EU restrictions on Chinese companies or products.

In an exclusive interview with Euronews last month, Sefčovič described the talks as highly political and said negotiations had to produce concrete results. Without them, he warned, there would be "a strong political movement to push for, I would say, harsher measures".

He also told Euronews that if he had nothing to show EU leaders, "the political interest would be to look for the solution through other instruments". Those leaders meet in Brussels on 15–16 October, a week after his trip.
